description: End-to-end scenario specifications with partial executable model evidence where noted. Structural checking is not execution.

scenarios.title: Letter through two relays and carried media
steps: Prepare a native signed letter offline with a stable Message-ID and two groups.
Accept locally, lose the reply, and retry.
Durably queue work for relay-a. Exercise an actual BPv7 contact outage and sender restart; restore contact, lose the application receipt, restart the receiver, and retry.
Resume through relay-b and carried media; import overlapping batches.
Commit matching release evidence while retaining independent archive pins.
expected: One article and one allocation per intended local membership.
Recovery restores obligations and permits receipt regeneration.
Local numbers may differ; transport reception does not imply human reading.
Bundle lifetime, expiry and transport status cannot release an fn application or archive obligation; destructive BPA deletion occurs only after durable fn staging.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial: actual two-node fn/BPv7 letter and return-receipt exchange, outage/restart, lost receipt and distinct-BID duplicate with one article/pin per node. Native signatures, two relays and carried-media composition remain open.

scenarios.title: Atomic cross-post and duplicate acceptance
steps: Prepare a two-group acceptance and observe before/after commit.
Retry the same identity and attempt a conflicting binding.
On the committed Store, compare an identical payload and ordered groups, then change payload, groups, and Message-ID separately.
expected: No partial membership is visible.
Retries allocate no numbers and do not overwrite accepted bytes.
Message-ID comparison is exact.
scenarios.execution_scope: Validated for abstract atomic acceptance; the native path is one article posted to two groups through the operator, one local number in each group across a restart, an identical resubmission accepted as the duplicate and a changed source under the held Message-ID refused without replacing the stored octets (tests/test_native_conformance.py). The charged pin is not observed by that case. The Python-host implementation (tests/test_store.py) retired with the Python host. Captured-caller source transport fixture additionally executes the actual native attempt before frontier: actual runtime source unavailable refuses before fill; synthetic unfunded retained callbacks preserve one shared remaining quantum and returned effects before fault. This fixture does not validate parser/provider authority, installed runtime allowance, all-alias retirement or the changed served image.

scenarios.title: Crash matrix around durable acceptance
steps: Crash at each object-write, namespace/barrier, commit-record, publication, and reply boundary.
Allow unsynced writes to tear/reorder within the selected model.
Recover and retry.
Exercise the fresh initializer with configuration history and repeated fresh staging names, and separate a removed configuration-directory fence from the root/transactions relation.
At native transaction recovery, supply a malformed final filename, a canonical filename hard-linked to a differently sequenced record, and a namespace exceeding its physical observation budget.
At native configuration recovery, supply a decoded-generation/basename mismatch, a canonical-looking symlink, a duplicate or gap, malformed bytes, and an entry beyond the physical observation budget.
expected: Modeled acknowledged commits survive; complete unacknowledged commits may survive.
No partial transaction is published.
Uncertainty fences mutations; platform assumptions are recorded.

Fresh successful initialization reaches the full image including durable configuration history; a weaker relation alone is not evidence of that publication. Transaction names come from the attached ACL2 renderer and remain distinct for distinct natural sequences.
Bound enumeration before retaining excess names; ACL2 owns canonical names and contiguous sequence pairs, and each decoded record must match its issued sequence before replay.

The configuration observer retains every bounded physical entry until ACL2 has decoded it and bound its generation to the canonical name. A conflicting, malformed, gapped, duplicate, excess, unreadable, or non-regular entry faults recovery rather than being filtered into a shorter history.
scenarios.execution_scope: Mixed actual node/file trace retention and observed replay/barrier gates have targeted certification. Forty-seven injection rows, six process-death cuts and sixteen malformed-image cases exercise the adapter. These finite tests do not qualify physical power loss or whole-store rollback. The deploy gate adds one real process-death cut on a farm box (SIGKILL from inside an open POST, recovery, reread); it is one point of the matrix, not the matrix, and a SIGKILL is not a power loss. W13 adds exact fresh-initializer image and transaction-name component evidence. Existing/retry initialization, native execution correspondence and coverage of every syscall/death cut remain open. W18 adds explicit existing-valid and history-fenced retry programs with EEXIST observations, plus source-pinned native repeated-init and SIGKILL/reopen tests. Non-EEXIST publication errors are uncertain. These are selected branch/runtime results, not whole-host or power-loss correspondence; the followup classifier covers expected-EEXIST links, and separate link/barrier handlers preserve uncertainty for post-link errors. Integrated raw-handler tests also exercise the named post-link error cut. Whole-image validation of these later corrections remains separate. Native U13 has source-matched developer Store-image malformed-name and sequence-binding witnesses plus raw observation bounds; it is not a full production-image, configuration-history or power-loss result.

scenarios.title: Checkpoint and complete index reconstruction
steps: Commit articles, allocations, obligations, receipts, and policy context.
Checkpoint and replay its suffix; rebuild indexes.
Compare exact lookups and ranges with full replay.
expected: All future-relevant state is preserved.
Range results are complete, not just individually valid.
Checkpoint choice does not depend on wall-clock recency.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial: logical checkpoint/suffix equivalence and index reconstruction are certified. Source-pinned native tests cover capture/select/reopen, selected corruption without rollback, unselected isolation, byte-identical cross-open, namespace bounds and selected crash cuts. The namespace successor adds unconditional mismatch corruption and mutation fencing. Recovery still fully replays the journal and compares a private restore; suffix-only recovery, full owner/index integration and every-cut physical correspondence remain open. A source-pinned ACL2 selected-pack witness additionally reconstructs E2 history/incarnation/sequence and bound hybrid keyring/historical verdict from exact event bytes; the version-two recovery-only checker also compares topic projection and the rebuilt consumer sequence index, rejecting mismatches. Combined native checkpoint/consumer/T10 reopen remains open.

scenarios.title: Interrupted compaction with active readers
steps: Create independent roots and pin a read on an old segment.
Compact under temporary-space pressure.
Crash around replacement publication and old-segment reclamation.
expected: Protected dependencies and evidence survive.
No-space causes safe refusal, not forced deletion.
Active readers retain required bytes; history policy persists.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial: selected lossless prefix packs reconstruct exact Store event bytes; focused tests cover corruption, missing selected authority, crash after a prefix unlink, resumed reclamation, and suffix replay. A certified pack-retirement plan excludes selected authority and models arbitrary survival after issued unlinks. Native source tests cover pack-retirement cuts, retry, exact source preservation, and active-reader refusal; pack-retirement awaits a source-matched developer image. The b074f94e developer-image fixture confirms active-reader exclusion before pack-reclaim unlink and exact source/retention preservation after release, reclamation and reopen (planning/evidence/checkpoint-active-reader-b074-2026-09-24.md). General concurrent physical reclamation, article-object reclamation, every physical cut, and filesystem qualification remain open.

scenarios.title: Corruption and old valid snapshots
steps: Inject detectable corruption in referenced content and committed metadata.
Attempt reading/recovery.
Separately replace the whole store by an older internally valid snapshot.
expected: Detected damage follows an explicit fault/repair path.
Damaged content cannot generate fresh success.
Rollback detection is claimed only with an independent freshness anchor.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial: actual checksum/truncation/unknown-schema/gap/symlink faults refuse recovery; replacement by a whole valid old store is intentionally undetected without an external anchor.

scenarios.title: Capacity refusal and indefinite local retention
steps: Fill the configured article/metadata reservation budget.
Attempt new work.
Advance wall time without authorization, then release one eligible archive pin.
expected: Unaffordable work is refused before acceptance.
Local archive pins do not expire automatically.
One release does not discharge unrelated obligations.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial: ledger and node retention proofs, real adapter bounds/maximum-profile replay, and BP receiver capacity refusal preserving prior article/archive pin. No durable deletion/compaction or physical disk-reservation proof.

scenarios.title: Lost, stale, and mismatched receipts
steps: Persist a successor undertaking and drop its reply.
Restart, retry, and regenerate the receipt.
Inject duplicates and wrong-subject/issuer/incarnation receipts.
expected: Undertakings do not multiply or vanish on restart.
Only matching sufficient authorized evidence permits discharge.
Socket ACKs and transmission reports do not release obligations.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial: actual receiver undertaking and receipt decision survive reopen; distinct-BID duplicate regenerates identical receipt and real BP returns it to a durably reopened sender. Five actual receiver SIGKILL cuts verify exact staged request/article, single record/article/pin, explicit pending recovery and identical receipts. Joint sender binding and fixed-Store receiver decision/replay/receipt-byte invariants are certified with nonvacuity and rejected-extension cases. Authenticated remote evidence, changing-Store composition and general journal-byte/host refinement remain open. The later native owner/FNRJ join independently exercises death after durable decision and before receipt authorship, then exact receipt replay after restart/retransmit without additional Store transaction/article/pin. Earlier fixed-Store theorems do not by themselves prove the new evolving-Store host composition. A later actual receipt-decision namespace-barrier EIO case observes uncertain exit with no receipt, then fresh-process recovery and exact receipt replay without additional Store acceptance.

scenarios.title: Reordered overlapping partial batches
steps: Import overlapping batches in several orders with duplicates.
Delay dependencies and resume partial objects.
Include competing claims under one news identity.
expected: Validated fact sets converge under stated hypotheses.
Incomplete dependency closure has no complete-acceptance receipt.
Local policies/numbers may differ and conflict evidence persists.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial: four-node validated fact merging/conflicts plus bounded volatile object assembly with reordered fragments, duplicates, gaps, conservative overlap conflict, byte/fragment/metadata limits and explicit empty candidates. No persistent transfer, selected portable batch grammar, dependency closure or acceptance receipts.

scenarios.title: Long asymmetric contacts and clock jumps
steps: Queue letters and receipts during a long outage.
Offer a brief one-way contact using cached inventory, then a return contact.
Jump wall time and vary permitted capacity/fairness.

After two durable local BP receives, make the older carrier clock-uncertain while the newer carrier is live; select and deliver the newer without changing the older. Also leave only the uncertain carrier, and separately make the FNBS publication outcome uncertain.
expected: Useful bounded batches need no preliminary dialogue.
Clock jumps do not discharge promises or prove non-delivery.
Progress assumptions and BP/fn lifetime distinctions are explicit.
Per-carrier clock uncertainty does not block a different live local delivery, while an uncertain publication still fences mutation.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial: real queued BP delivery after contact outage and process restart, sender retry semantics and finite transport-safety proofs. The local A3 clocked selector has a certified two-receive ACL2 trace, with no source-matched native image for that change. Asymmetric scheduled windows, wall-clock jumps, LTP and fairness/liveness remain open.

scenarios.title: Restore incarnations and forks
steps: Issue origin events and retain an older backup.
Restore/clone that backup after more events circulate.
Attempt issuance and exchange competing histories.
expected: Restore discipline prevents unrecognized identity reuse under A-IDENTITY.
Fork evidence remains; timestamps do not settle authority.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial: ACL2 clone proposal/phase tests certify, and native source implements a pre-open fence, no-replace cold copy and durable rollover/reopen. The saved-image fixture and process-death cuts are written but await a combined E2 image; competing origin forks and served cursor rejection remain open.

scenarios.title: Source variants, signatures, and authority
steps: Import native signed content, gateway provenance, and legacy wire variants.
Change Path/Xref and gateway injection projections while keeping exact authored source octets, including unknown allowed headers and MIME bytes; separately alter signed source content.
Present unrelated signatures and forged administrative requests.

Render the selected FN-Authorship carrier from independently supplied Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 keys, verify the received article, then alter one exact source byte and one encoded public-key byte separately.
expected: Provenance categories remain distinct.
The selected signing preimage binds exact authored source bytes. Changing mutable projections does not rewrite those bytes; changing authored content is not a projection-only change.
Relay mutation and authored conflict are distinguished; unrelated signers gain no authority.
The portable verifier accepts only the intact both-signature artifact and refuses each altered variant; its result is distinct from a Store historical verdict.
scenarios.design_note: D01 selects this source boundary and the FN-Authorship v1 carrier implements a bounded portable artifact check. The native CLI source/keyset mutation witness covers only that check; Store binding, served HDR and peer transit remain open.

scenarios.title: Codec vectors and hostile declarations
steps: Round-trip schema boundary values.
Supply duplicate keys, alternate encodings, truncation, huge lengths, deep nesting, and unknown versions.
Compare bytes with an independent implementation.
expected: Accepted values have the specified deterministic encodings.
Resource checks precede allocation; input is never evaluated as Lisp.
Unknown schemas cannot establish semantic authority.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial: primitive/schema-0 round trips and accepted-input canonicality, 38 independent cbor2 cases, malformed-store vectors, exact article preservation/recognized bounded syntax, semantic fields, UTF-8/wildmat correspondence, and CBOR/record guards. Native/batch/signature schema and full public resource proofs remain open.

scenarios.title: NNTP cursor, capabilities, and framing
steps: Exercise advertised forms with a real reader and independent transcripts.
Partition CRLF, dot terminators, and articles across socket chunks.
Exercise empty/missing groups, IDs, cursors, ranges, wildmat, failed selection, and oversized input.

Poll with NEWNEWS over a wildmat and a date, with and without GMT and with both year forms, against stamped articles whose payloads carry Injection-Date, Date, and neither, plus carried-over legacy articles.
expected: Capability claims match the audited profile.
Cursor/errors follow the checklist.
Socket partitions do not change meaning; rejected body tails do not become commands.

NEWNEWS names exactly the matching groups' articles at or after the requested acceptance stamp or conservative legacy horizon, without reading payloads or a size refusal; syntax and two-digit-year clock refusals stay distinct.
scenarios.execution_scope: Implemented reader session/cursor and effect shape have general proofs; exact ACL2 bridge input partitions and real reconnects have targeted tests. Full READER/POST and complete RFC byte-response conformance remain open. Framing and cursor coverage moved from the host to books/served, which states chunk-partition independence of the function the host calls. The capabilities leg is REFUTED as it stands: the deploy gate found POST answered with 340 while CAPABILITIES omits POST (RFC 3977 section 5.2.2).

scenarios.title: Host replay, stale completion, and backpressure
steps: Replay traces in the model simulator and core/host integration.
Deliver stale/duplicate completions.
Force partial output and stalled readers.

Install and exercise the native CLI and two native nodes without a Python runtime; include startup, concurrent NNTP posting/peering, control/reconfiguration, BP work, selected identity/anchor operations and crash recovery.
Record native image/source/dependency identities and child-process executions; distinguish an external test harness from either deployed node.

With two native owner clients already connected, inject uncertainty after publication on one client while the other attempts further input; then exercise shared-resource shutdown and independent recovery.
Start two distinct Store roots with one control socket path; issue concurrent native control posts and then repeat SIGTERM while NNTP and partial control clients are connected.
Send control frames in one-byte fragments and stall them; exceed the active control-client ceiling while a valid client continues; drop a post reply after durable completion and reopen independently.

On production default and DTN images, invoke raw store ROOT post with fresh and existing Store roots and an observable payload path; attempt a runtime profile override. Repeat raw insertion on the developer image, then exercise ordinary operator/NNTP posting, inspection and recovery on production.

For store ROOT probe COUNT [article], repeat production default/DTN refusal with fresh and existing roots; test direct handler refusal before store construction and developer handler availability. Malformed COUNT values must produce usage errors.
expected: Stale completions cannot publish another transaction.
Finishing writes does not rerun semantic transitions.
Effects remain bounded and the same core/declared trust boundary is used.
No deployed entry point, helper or recovery path requires Python or silently falls back to the Python owner; missing native features remain open.
The native owner calls the same ACL2 semantic subjects or named justified refinements and preserves accepted, refused, uncertain and fault outcomes.

The uncertainty fence is established before releasing the shared mutex; no connected or newly arriving client mutates the stopped owner, workers finish before shared resources close, and the process reports uncertainty distinctly from a core fault.

A live store prepare may omit repeated history replay only through a named equality to fn-sn-prepare whose invariant is established at observed open and preserved by every post-open mutator; the shared owner additionally requires a named equality to its actual configured-owner event and exact preservation of owner/configuration context.

Only the endpoint lease holder receives control submissions; shutdown wakes clients without closing descriptors beneath their workers, joins before releasing resources, and permits independent reopen.

Control transport bounds active clients and total frame time, bounds allocation before consuming excess bytes, and accumulates input in linear work; a lost post reply is uncertain and a retry cannot duplicate durable acceptance.

Production raw insertion exits 5 as an unsupported entry before Store or payload I/O, regardless of a runtime profile override; no publication occurs. Developer raw insertion remains available. Ordinary production submission still injects and preserves its accepted/refused/uncertain contract, and production inspection/recovery remain available. This selected 2026-09-23 requirement is not yet implemented or witnessed by da5fd8cb.

Production capacity probes refuse before writable-store construction or fixture publication. The developer handler remains available; malformed COUNT uses the operator decimal-natural usage outcome. Extracted-source checks do not substitute for matching saved-image tests.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial: frozen03 default/DTN builds and scoped native suites passed, including public operator startup and concurrent uncertainty fencing. Later logical traces and targeted native tests cover stated subcontracts. The standalone store and shared-owner prepare projections are certified equal to their replaying specification/previous owner event under maintained relations, with nonempty-history witnesses and stale-node counterexamples when the premises are removed. A production image at 8cbeda9 passed all six targeted native-owner tests, including durable POST/reopen and uncertainty fencing. The frozen cdbd6b2 Python service matrix retains its recorded authentication and BP-crash disagreements. Full native service parity, deployment dependency evidence, concurrent backpressure/stale-completion composition and complete physical adapter correspondence remain open; the targeted owner image is not the whole deployment gate. The integrated control packet has ACL2 closure and exact-raw Darwin lifecycle/posting evidence; its saved-image build returned nonzero due to unrelated certificate origins, so it is not a clean native build gate. The later control resource packet passed scoped native slow-drip and active-client ceiling cases; it adds linear accumulation by source inspection, with the combined image gate still separate.

scenarios.title: History pruning and ancient reimport
steps: Release an eligible archive pin while retaining history.
Apply selected pruning rules and reimport old carried media.
Try to reuse an allocated local article number.
expected: Reimport follows the explicit resurrection/admissibility policy.
No other article reuses an allocation.
Independent obligations and evidence survive visibility changes.

scenarios.title: BP adapter acceptance separation
steps: Carry a real versioned batch through a selected BP implementation.
Observe transport status before application acceptance.
Expire a bundle or interrupt its path and retry.
Receive a nonzero fragment, restart, then receive offset zero and reassemble only from a complete coherent live family.
Reopen an FNWF journal interleaving ION route/observation records with application attempt, receipt and release records.

For the ION adapter, undertake the canonical Store forward pin, submit through the explicit application/BP route, and reopen the durable observation. Refuse fractional or out-of-helper-range lifetime before publishing any attempt or launching the helper; entered-send observation failures stay uncertain.

Complete a multi-quantum fragment family: final custody ACK precedes reassembly, a keepalive/input turn resumes one quantum, EOF moves pending work to listener turns, and diagnostic once drains only after socket closure.
Open BP budgets with missing/default and ASCII rows; refuse repeated owner-backoff/retry-budget, unknown keys, malformed or non-ASCII decimal input before running a node.
expected: Transport status is not a retention undertaking.
Only validated complete application inputs receive matching receipts.
No fragment enters Store before durable whole-bundle replacement; expired or unknown-age source rows cannot be silently omitted from that replacement.
Adapter version, lifetime profile, and interoperability evidence are recorded.

Successful mixed-journal replay preserves application work status with one restart, while ION observations remain separate from receipt/release authority; PRF-034 actual-caller correspondence is still open.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial: the actual pinned BPA exchange carries an experimental whole-article ADU and matching receipt through outage/restart/lost receipt/duplicate retry. Sender and receiver logical assurance and five receiver process-death cuts have separate evidence. Complete portable batches, explicit expiry/contact/quota cases, authenticated handoff and additional CLA profiles remain open. Moved to M4 to match the user's A06 active BP path; status remains specified. Native TCPCL request-to-owner-Store-to-receipt composition has a separate loopback restart witness; it is not external BPA interoperability or a complete contact-plan test. The fragment-carrier and observation-bound kind-18 transitions have ACL2 evidence; the two-process interrupted-fragment native fixture awaits a source-matched saved image. The optional offline ION sender has a certified ACL2 observation/route/replay component and a source-present native caller; native image qualification, real death/reopen and receipt-return over ION remain open.
scenarios.notes: Retained TCPCL actual-driver recording fixture distinguishes partial/wait writes, ACK-write-before-progress, pump/input interleaving, source-owned input, EOF/deadline loss, and publication errors that escape the socket scope. Matching saved-image execution remains pending.

scenarios.title: Private-profile design and crypto integration exercise
steps: Model trusted endpoints, opaque relay storage, and exposed metadata.
Walk through partitioned membership changes, delayed epochs, archive recovery, and secret-state rollback.
Compare candidate protocol requirements; later repeat using the selected implementation before shipping privacy.
expected: D04/D09 choices have an explicit threat model and no invented ratchet construction.
Ciphertext obligations do not require indefinite retention of all group secrets.
Membership ordering, signatures, archive recovery, and metadata leakage have separate stated semantics.
M1 evidence is a design exercise only; actual private-profile integration remains a later release gate.

scenarios.title: Two-node statement exchange through a peer that does not understand it
steps: Give node A and node B separate keyrings, both holding agent A's public key, and configure one relay between them that knows nothing about FN-Statement.
Agent A signs a statement over its authored source bytes and posts the article to node A with the statement in the FN-Statement header field.
Relay the article A -> relay -> B, capturing the octets at each hop.
On node B, fetch the article with ARTICLE and HEAD and verify the signature with an independent client that uses its own keyring and no fn code.
Ask node B for HDR :fn-verified over the article's range and over its Message-ID.
Repeat with the article's body altered by one octet in transit, with an article whose creator node B does not know, and with an article carrying no FN-Statement.
Offer node B a policy statement for a group the offering peer does not govern, then the genuine authority's policy statement, comparing the policy in force before and after each batch.
Have agent A reissue one (incarnation, sequence) slot with two different payloads, deliver one fork to each node, then peer the two nodes both ways.
Partition two sites, remove a different member at each, reconnect, and merge the reconnected peer's commits.
expected: The FN-Statement field arrives at node B byte-identical; only Path and Xref differ across the hops.
The independent client verifies the signature from the served bytes alone, without asking fn for a verdict.
HDR :fn-verified reports verified with the principal id in hex and the keyring generation under which the verdict was computed.

The altered body yields unverified ref-mismatch, the unknown creator unverified signature, and the missing field absent no-field; all three articles are still accepted, stored byte-exact and served, and no two of the outcomes render as one token.
The offering peer's policy statement leaves the policy in force equal before and after; the genuine authority's changes it, and the changing statement is named.
Both nodes end holding both forks and report the creator as an equivocator, with the durable equivocation record agreeing with the lace.
After the reconnection merge every earlier admit/refuse/hold decision is unchanged and the fork is exposed with both removals present.
No run here is proof evidence: it exercises the design's acceptance criteria against books that do not exist at this revision.

scenarios.title: A provenance survives the store, and a legacy one keeps its meaning
steps: Post one article to a fresh store; ACL2 decides the provenance from the live configuration and hands the host the form the record grammar accepts.
Close the store and reopen it, which replays the journal into a fresh node.
Ask the node for the provenance of that Message-ID and for the provenance of a value written before the typed record existed.
Ask for the provenance of a Message-ID the node does not hold.
expected: The stored evidence is the canonical wire form: prefixed, printable in octets 33 to 126, and at most 256 octets, so the host boundary guard and the record grammar both admit it.
The provenance read back after the reopen is the provenance the acceptance recorded, field for field.
A value written before the typed record existed reads back as the :legacy kind, verbatim, and renders as the string it always rendered as.
A Message-ID the node does not hold is a refusal (exit 1), distinct from uncertainty (exit 3) and a fault (exit 4).
scenarios.note: The transit path is NOT covered: it still stores fn-peer-evidence's rendering. See planning/lanes/HANDOFF-w10-provenance.md.

scenarios.title: Two peered nodes stand up, reconfigure live, and stop
steps: Initialize each node from the operator surface: a store, its served groups, and a configuration file naming the store, the listener and the ACL2 image.
Report each node's status; initialize over an existing store again; reject a wildcard listener configuration before bind with a usage result.
Create and retire a served group, and observe the created group over the socket.
Start each node's service, declare a group on the running service's control channel, and attempt the same change through the offline command while the service holds the store.
Stop each service and reopen each store.
expected: Every command's exit code distinguishes accepted, refused and uncertain, and no command reports an outcome the store did not take.
A configuration written by the operator surface is the one the service reads; nothing infers a store path from the working directory.
A change made while the service is live reaches the served configuration through the control channel, and the offline path is refused rather than racing it.
A stopped service releases the writer lock, and the store reopens without recovery.
scenarios.execution_scope: Specified. The v0 rows (planning/v0-matrix.json, last run b6759850) are owned by tests/test_native_conformance.py on one node and by tests/test_native_peering.py and tests/test_native_protected_peering.py between two nodes on one host over loopback (planning/evidence/python-diet-2-2026-09-28/v0-row-owners.md). Nothing here exercises two machines, a real network, or an operator's own configuration.

scenarios.title: AUTHINFO login and posting permission
steps: Derive a principal from a seed and record an AUTHINFO credential for it on each node.
Connect unauthenticated and read the advertised capabilities; attempt a gated command.
Authenticate with AUTHINFO USER and PASS, read the capabilities again, and post.
Authenticate with a wrong password on a fresh connection.
Run one complete served read with a nonempty no-posting credential list: AUTHINFO USER/PASS then local POST, and separately AUTHINFO USER/PASS then configured-peer TAKETHIS with an article body.
expected: AUTHINFO USER is advertised exactly while the connection is unauthenticated, and is withdrawn once it is not.
A gated command before the login is refused and not performed.
The posting allowance is the authenticated principal's, not the connection's.
A wrong password is refused and grants nothing; the refusal is distinct from a fault.

The no-posters served-read invariant excludes every local injected submission, but the independently authorized principal-bound transit path may emit a typed peer submission; removing the no-posters premise allows a complete accepted local POST.
A policy-switched pending POST state can submit despite a no-posters credential policy, but cannot arise from an initial no-posters connection under the proved fold invariant.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial native evidence: startup loads bounded credential verifiers, required unauthenticated command returns 480, wrong password returns 481, correct password returns 281 and subsequent GROUP succeeds; authenticated reader IHAVE remains 502. Protected-only startup and legacy cleartext credential files refuse. Login transport is unprotected loopback, so no confidentiality claim follows. Native credential enrollment, TLS, reload and full cross-node scenario remain separate. The served-fold distinction between local POST and authorized transit is ACL2-certified with reachable complete-read witnesses; no new native transcript is claimed by that component evidence.

scenarios.title: Transit between two peered fn nodes in both directions
steps: Peer each node with the other by a record naming its path-identity, its transport and its inbound and outbound wildmats.
Establish the control: each node serves its own article and refuses the other's.
Offer one article each way with IHAVE, then offer the same Message-ID a second time, then offer one whose Path already names the target.
Offer a further article each way with MODE STREAM, CHECK and TAKETHIS, and repeat the offer after the target holds it.
expected: A wanted offer draws 335 and then 235, and the target serves the source's octets with its own path-identity and the RFC 5537 section 3.2.1 diagnostic prepended to Path and every Xref removed, every other header and the body byte-identical (specs/peering.md 2.3); local article numbers may differ.
A second offer of a held Message-ID draws 435 and no second copy is written.
An article whose Path already names the target is refused after its 335 and is not served afterwards.
CHECK answers 238 for a wanted article and 438 for one the target holds; TAKETHIS answers 239 and 439 to match, never a 2xx and never a retry code.
A peer record is configuration, not authorization: nothing in this scenario authenticates the peer.
scenarios.execution_scope: A source-matched production image ran two native owners on one host over private loopback. Public operator configuration drove byte-identical A-to-B and B-to-A transfers, and each held Message-ID drew 435. A separate client reset while a transit completed; the target retained the article and stayed live, but the test did not observe whether the reply write itself failed. The run did not exercise TLS, two hosts, a partition, latency or clock disagreement, and two articles crossing once is not the merge property of specs/peering.md section 4.

scenarios.title: Owner-driven outbound feed
steps: Configure an outbound wildmat on a peer record and accept an article that matches it.
Let the owner open the session and offer the article; drive no socket by hand.
Reread the target after the acknowledgement, and again after the source restarts.
Interrupt an offer in flight and restart the owner.
Cut a following FNFD envelope at each byte boundary, reopen, append and reopen again.
Offer complete corrupt or wrong-peer FNFD evidence, and inject failed content/directory barriers.
expected: Each accepted article is offered to each peer whose outbound wildmat matches it, by the owner and not by an operator.
A transfer the target acknowledged is not offered again, and the target holds one copy.
The feed journal distinguishes transmission from retention, and survives the restart.
An interrupted offer is retried and produces no second copy.
Only a torn final envelope is truncated to the ACL2-returned safe offset; a later append remains replayable after another restart.
Complete invalid evidence remains unchanged; ambiguous I/O exits uncertain and the owner performs no later mutation or success response.
scenarios.execution_scope: The owner drives outbound feeds; the former standalone tools/run_feed.py is retired. A source-matched production image ran the combined public operator, owner, feed and inbound NNTP path over private loopback. It transferred one article byte-identically in each direction, suppressed both duplicates, and requeued a durable FNFD obligation after the source process was killed and restarted. W12 separately covers bounded journal replay and cuts. Article-commit/feed-intent atomicity and general K5 correspondence remain active work, so the whole scenario is not marked validated.

scenarios.title: A bundle each way over fn's own convergence layer
steps: Build the node image carrying the convergence layer and establish a contact between two of them.
Transfer one bundle each way inside one session, segmented by the layer's own rules.
Interrupt the contact and re-establish it; hold an idle contact open with the keepalive.
Carry an fn article inside a bundle and deliver it to the receiving node's application.
Inject errors at native lifecycle publication barriers, reopen, and distinguish a visible record from durable queue acceptance.
Reuse a session-local transfer ID in another inbound session with different content; retain both evidence records and fence all mutation after an uncertain journal write.
expected: The transfer is segmented and acknowledged by the layer's own rules, and the assertions are over the events the layer recorded.
A bundle's arrival is not an fn application acceptance, and the two are reported separately.
An interrupted contact retains durably queued work; transport retries may repeat a bundle, while application acceptance and obligation charging remain idempotent.
A refused contact is refused with its own reason, distinct from a fault.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial: native BP codec/node and durable outbound lifecycle execute behind TCPCL. Source-pinned packets cover sequence allocation, spool recovery, selected process-death cuts and lifecycle publication/restart. W15 adds actual cross-session transfer-ID reuse with both wires retained, receive-loop exit after uncertain publication, and wire-only evidence identity consumption after recovery barriers. The allocation theorem is conditional on confirmed-frontier admissibility. Full native application journal/receipt composition and universal actual-host lifecycle/physical refinement remain open (PRF-045/046). Receive evidence enumeration now enforces the ACL2 bound during collection; its actual raw directory regression passed on integrated 7a0b96f. This is not a newly built combined image test.

scenarios.title: A host fault on one connection, with another connection open across it
steps: Start the owner (`owner run STORE 0 0 8 connectionhandler`, the developer image's test-only injector armed at the connection handler's receive).
Open three connections; the first one's read reaches the armed point, so its handler raises an exception the host does not expect.
Serve the second connection (opened before the fault) and post from the third; open a fourth after the fault and read the posted article.
expected: The faulted connection receives the model's 403 internal-fault line and nothing else, and the server closes it (EOF, no octet pending).
The other connection is served at the pin it already held, and a connection opened after the fault is served too and reads the new article.
A post from another connection reaches 240, so the fault did not wedge the writer, and the owner is still running.
scenarios.execution_scope: Re-implemented natively (row L2, lane small-rows, 2026-09-29) over the connection-local handler fault. The Python host's second case, an exception inside the writer step after the article reached the submission queue, is retired with that host: in the native owner a fault in the shared writer is the shared-state global fence (SCN-015), never a per-connection fault, so that case has no native counterpart. The earlier implementation was tests/test_owner.py OwnerSurvivesAFaultTests over the retired Python host (recoverable at 940bc3104).

scenarios.title: Atomic signed acceptance across refusal, burned allocation and restart
steps: Enroll one exact hybrid key snapshot, sign an exact source with Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65, commit one schema-1 atomically bound received-carrier article plus historical verdict, and reopen the Store.
Reserve and refuse another transaction so the allocator transaction ID advances without advancing the Store journal sequence.
Commit later Store events, reopen again, and query the historical verdicts.
At the shared native publication helper, inject an expected prepublication refusal and then a valid operation; separately inject indeterminate and structural-fault outcomes.
Open a structurally bound kind-4 history whose embedded article replays but whose historical enrollment is missing.
expected: The kind-4 received article and historical verdict appear together after both reopens; its separately retained exact authored source and identity agree with the carrier projection and the enrolled ordered key set.
The burned allocator ID creates no journal-sequence gap and does not prevent later recovery.
A legacy article has no reconstructed historical verdict because its record contains no immutable verdict evidence.
Expected refusal consumes the reservation and permits the following valid commit; indeterminate and structural faults remain fenced and are never reported as refusal.
Identity recovery failure leaves the retained history intact, returns the composed replay error, and cannot reach ready through recovery barriers.
scenarios.execution_scope: The existing ACL2 source trace executes fn-sn transitions and reopen, and the raw SBCL witness executes the shared publication helper with controlled observations. The new schema-1 codec, constructor and substitution witnesses certify separately; the modified native hybrid-author/restart witness still needs a combined saved image. These results do not establish filesystem durability, cryptographic primitive correctness or arbitrary-trace preservation; PRF-050 remains in progress. The negative missing-enrollment composed trace evaluates from ACL2 sources, with no native corrupted-store startup claim.
scenarios.note: assurance-triage 2026-09-26: returned to specified: no recorded run of the SBCL witness (tests/native_owner_publication.lisp) or any native run; only the ACL2 book tests/acl2/store-identity-traces-tests is certified.

scenarios.title: Late TCPCL refusal replaces final ACK after partial segments
steps: Establish a native TCPCL session and send a transfer in at least three segments so two partial ACKs precede END.
Make the BP receive callback return a definitive capacity refusal after seeing the complete transfer; repeat with an ambiguous FNBS publication result.
On a valid durable received bundle and an exact already-durable duplicate, exercise the accepted callback result.
expected: The sender observes XFER_REFUSE No Resources and no successful final END ACK for the capacity refusal; already emitted partial ACKs do not complete the transfer.
Ambiguous publication releases no final ACK, fences the receiver, and does not appear as a definitive refusal or acceptance.
Only the durable new record or exact duplicate releases the final ACK; transport ACK alone never discharges an application receipt.
scenarios.execution_scope: ACL2 host-drive event ordering, two coalesced completions, held-prefix projection, and no-final-ACK planner proof are certified. The native partial-refusal regression is prepared but awaits a source-matched combined image and the A2 FNBS callback join; ambiguity and durable duplicate require that joined image.

scenarios.title: Persisted BP clock domain gates same-boot restart and incomparable boot counters
steps: Persist a received bundle with a short lifetime and an FNBS clock-domain marker, stop the BP process, wait beyond the lifetime, and reopen during the same Linux boot.
Restart with a valid marker for a different boot ID while supplying both a lower and a higher monotonic counter than the saved age anchor.
Reopen a legacy FNBS directory without a clock-domain marker, and inject a process death after the marker link but before its directory barrier.
expected: The same-boot process restart reads the exact 82-byte marker and uses CLOCK_BOOTTIME elapsed time, so the short-lifetime bundle is expired.
Both different-boot readings fence BP lifecycle before replay or expiry; no incomparable counter silently renews a TTL or fabricates expiry.
Missing legacy marker and ambiguous marker publication remain fenced, preserving obligations until an explicit recovery or migration policy resolves them.
scenarios.execution_scope: ACL2 marker codec, startup plan, and valid changed-boot counterexamples are certified. A source-matched full developer image passed same-boot expiry, corrupt and absent-legacy marker fences, and visible-marker directory-barrier recovery; the production image passed exact ADU transfer with markers at both ends. No physical alternate-boot run or cross-boot reanchor is claimed; changed-boot startup fences.

scenarios.title: Native signed article carries local Path through peer relay and receiver restart
steps: Enroll an exact hybrid key snapshot, sign exact authored source, and submit through native hybrid-author under an owner with a configured Path identity.
Read the source owner ARTICLE, then transfer it to a second native protected peer and restart the receiving owner.
Read the receiver ARTICLE and portable authorship verification after restart.
expected: The source ARTICLE has one Path from the local ACL2 injection and the native carrier still reconstructs the exact signed source.
The relay ARTICLE has the receiver Path entry prepended to that received Path; its other bytes and signed source are unchanged, with no re-signing.
The receiver retains one article and verifies the same historical authorship after restart.
scenarios.execution_scope: The ACL2 injected-byte projection, event-constructor witness and dependent Store books are certified. The existing real two-owner test first exposed the absent Path on the old image and remains a prepared regression until root builds and runs a matching combined image. A transport success by itself is not an authorship or durability proof.

scenarios.title: A signed exact-source topic candidate remains separate from authority
steps: Construct canonical root, control and report field candidates through the ACL2 codec in exact authored source; sign one source using the hybrid carrier and inspect it in the native CLI.
Add a mutable relay Path/Xref projection to the received carrier and inspect again.
Mutate a signed FN-Topic byte, duplicate the field, fold base64 inside the field, and supply malformed or oversized binary/base64 variants.
expected: Canonical values round-trip and a source-matched native inspection reports topic=candidate, carrier=authenticated, admission=unestablished.
Mutable relay headers leave exact-source metadata unchanged.
A signed-byte mutation fails carrier verification; duplicate, malformed, folded or over-limit metadata never becomes topic authority, including when an ordinary article is retained.
scenarios.execution_scope: ACL2 component tests certified, including the maximum root and malformed/duplicate/folding cases. A source-matched saved-image CLI test is prepared but not yet run; Store topic-event admission and current-policy status are outside this first slice.

scenarios.title: Sleeping-agent durable consumer progress across Store and inbox crashes
steps: Commit the immutable signed report in a separately administered Store while the consumer sleeps; register under a pinned history, incarnation, query and view, then query consumer status.
Poll a bounded page, atomically bind the exact source and operation identity to the consumer inbox and immutable reply outbox, then acknowledge only the scanned committed prefix.
Query status before and after ACK and after Store reopen; compare committed ACK, journal frontier and event distance without treating the distance as unread or application work.

At linked-but-unfinished Store records and consumer transaction/ack publication cuts, crash and reopen the Store and consumer database, settle uncertainty by querying both durable states, and repeat safely.
Replace or clone the endpoint with a fresh durable incarnation, change the authorization view, and offer old cursors and delayed acknowledgements before explicit rebase.
expected: Status returns only a registered consumer's committed ACK position, committed journal frontier and their ACL2-computed difference in Store events. It does not poll, mutate progress, or scan retained history.
The Store position is unchanged by poll or reply generation and advances only on a durable consumer ack declaration.
After recovery, Store progress equals replay of the committed prefix; the consumer has neither or both inbox/outbox records at its transaction cut and one operation-index result.
A linked Store candidate is either absent or replayed once at recovery; no stale live projection is accepted as progress.
Old incarnation, registration epoch and view cursors are refused without mutation; independent stores and consumers keep separate positions.
scenarios.note: The ACL2 Store model is witnessed by tests/acl2/consumer-store-invariants-tests.lisp and its scoped manifest. Native image 1d26e01f passed signed local-owner poll, read-only repeat, advancing ACK with killed reply/reopen and fenced clone cursor recovery, as recorded in planning/evidence/native-poll-reader-clone-1d26-2026-09-23.md. The local consumer-status command is an experimental v1 diagnostic and has no v0 gate. The Mini consumer-owned transaction/ACK/reply join and complete two-store E2-01.. trace set remain unqualified; component passes do not establish the whole scenario.

scenarios.title: Topic candidate author comes from verified exact source and historical key context
steps: Select a canonical root with a controller and keyset ID matching the verified hybrid principal and ordered key snapshot; repeat with changed principal and changed keyset under the same principal.
Select a report whose From claims another author and a received relay projection with a competing FN-Topic field.

Construct a retained schema-1 article event and matching historical keyring snapshot; repeat with changed enrolled principal and substituted retained exact source. Inspect a signed carrier in the native CLI.
expected: Only the exact matching root receives controller-matched status; either verified-context change yields controller-mismatch while generic topic candidate reporting remains available.
The report author reference is derived from verified principal and ordered keys; From and relay fields do not supply author authority.

The matching retained event selects its exact-source candidate; historical enrollment or source substitution returns unbound-event. Native output retains topic=candidate and admission=unestablished with verifier-derived author/binding fields.
scenarios.execution_scope: ACL2 constructor, selector, historical event and negative teeth tests certify on hbox at the lane source. The updated native CLI awaits a source-matched combined saved image; no durable topic admission, fork choice, roster adoption or general signature primitive proof is claimed.

scenarios.title: Pinned LISTGROUP and OVER ranges use matching historical group buckets
steps: Commit a sparse local-number membership, retain an earlier reader, and open a new reader after the commit.
Send the same LISTGROUP group/range octets through fn-own-read on both connections.
Construct a malformed tagged pin with a correct Message-ID trie but missing group bucket; compare its command result with the archive command.
Construct 24 unrelated groups and measure selected bucket work against the flat membership list.
Send sparse OVER and empty XOVER ranges through the pinned ACL2 dispatcher; compare the complete result with the archive dispatcher and repeat with stale bucket and missing trie pins.

On a source-matched saved image, retain readers across live group creation and three posts, then restart; issue bounded LISTGROUP ranges through the socket and measure 96 range reads over a declared 24-group, 24-article workload.
On that image, post a crosspost and two group-specific articles while keeping old and new readers pinned; issue OVER and XOVER ranges concurrently, then restart and repeat.
expected: The older reader sees its old empty group and the new reader sees exactly the committed sparse local number in a correctly framed multiline reply.
The malformed pin changes the answer and fails the maintained pin correspondence predicate.
The selected head bucket visits two units (one header and one entry) against 24 flat memberships; no timing or sort bound is inferred.
The indexed OVER/XOVER replies equal the archive replies, including 423 versus legacy 420 on empty ranges; either malformed pin changes the answer.

Old readers retain their configured and committed view, the fresh reader and restarted owner return only their visible local numbers, and the declared socket timing is reported without an asymptotic claim. An internal deletion/allocation hole remains unexercised because the public operator surface cannot create one.

OVER and XOVER return the same exact crosspost overview line in each visible group, old pins hide later posts, bounded and high-empty ranges retain their response codes, concurrent readers agree, and restart recovers the latest view.
scenarios.execution_scope: ACL2 owner-called LISTGROUP and pinned OVER/XOVER paths have scoped farm certification, including sparse historical replies, malformed pin counterexamples, and distinct empty-range codes. Native historical/config/restart LISTGROUP and crosspost, pinned, concurrent OVER/XOVER drivers are prepared for root’s next source-matched saved image; neither has run on this lane. No native OVER/XOVER timing or internal allocation-hole claim is made.

scenarios.title: Experimental root anchor and report proposal respects T10, roster, parents and quota
steps: From an already accepted schema-1 root and historical key snapshot, prepare and commit a finite local anchor under the installed administrator ID. Repeat with a different caller, changed snapshot and the same already anchored root.

Construct an accepted report signed by a roster author, propose and commit its admission, then retry the exact source after the finite quota is consumed and after native Store reopen; compare transaction filenames and bytes before and after each retry.
Construct separate accepted reports under a non-roster signer, with an unadmitted same-topic parent and after quota exhaustion. Compare the projection before preparation and after completion.
Complete a valid administrator install, anchor and report in Store; reopen the completed prefix, then try a structurally valid duplicate administrator install image.
expected: Only the matching administrator/root context yields a proposed anchor; the same root cannot be anchored twice.

The report receives one historical admission. Exact retry returns a distinct successful replayed-historical status with no admission bytes over control, no second Store event and no additional charge, including after reopen; proposal alone does not change state.
Non-roster author, missing parent and no remaining quota each refuse fresh admission; no ordinary article acceptance is undone.
Completed topic events advance Store sequence/transaction and carried topic state while preserving article acceptance; observed reopen rejects the duplicate-install topic history with :replay.
scenarios.execution_scope: Scoped v2 codec, prefix, owner-called proposal, Store prepare and source-vector ACL2 roots passed on persvati. The pre-v2 b074 image is qualified and retained. The prepared dual-image v1-to-v2/mixed-history native test, v2 saved image, whole reverse closure, and maintained topic/crash relation have not yet qualified.

scenarios.title: Durable local human submission without automatic repost
steps: Compose one article with a persistent outbox, race two HTTP POST handlers, restart the web client, and submit the same identifier again.
Save an incomplete editable draft, restart, edit and save it again, then Post the final source once.
Lose the NNTP reply after article bytes, restart with both a recorded uncertain reply and a bare in-flight intent, and make a read-only ARTICLE settlement observation.
Inject outbox-parent, draft, file and directory fsync failures before and after the NNTP attempt, then fill the bounded spool.
expected: The exact source, Message-ID and target are frozen before the sole NNTP attempt; duplicate handlers and restart do not repost.
A saved draft survives restart without a Message-ID or network attempt; Post freezes only the final submitted fields.
In-flight and lost-reply outcomes remain uncertain; an ARTICLE lookup records only what is currently served.

A parent or intent write failure sends no article; a reply-record write failure retains the known node answer in the running process and fences new submissions; a full spool preserves all prior records.
scenarios.execution_scope: Real local HTTP and fake NNTP socket tests exercise this separate client's behavior. A source-matched native-node run, physical power-loss qualification, and general external-web security audit remain open.
scenarios.note: Retired 2026-09-28 (lane web-native-2) with tools/fn_web.py and tools/fn_reader.py: the web page is the node's own face (WEB-005). This scenario ran against the Python reader; its record stays as history.

scenarios.title: Local hybrid author rotation and revocation preserve unrelated and historical authority
steps: Enroll A at generation 1 and B at generation 2; authorize fresh signed sources from both after B is enrolled.
Rotate A at generation 3; try a new correctly signed A source under generation 1, then accept one under generation 3.
Revoke A at generation 4; try a newly signed A source under generation 3 and a fresh B source under generation 2.
Stop the owner, reopen the Store, inspect the ordered key history and the first accepted A article's recorded verdict. Independently verify its portable carrier.
expected: B enrollment does not retire A; only A's old generation loses new local author permission on rotation.
The tombstone refuses new A authorship while B remains authorized; malformed/wrong-principal/old-generation lifecycle requests refuse without publishing.
Historical A snapshot and kind-4 verdict remain unchanged after reopen; portable artifact verification is separate from current local permission.
scenarios.execution_scope: ACL2 source tests cover ordered snapshot/replay and the control codec. The opt-in native owner, saved-image and restart fixture is source-present but not yet qualified on a matching image; no remote revocation or cryptographic succession policy follows.

scenarios.title: Protected peer carrier becomes a receiver-local historical authorship event
steps: Enroll the exact principal and ordered hybrid keys at receiving node B, transfer A's signed carrier over a configured protected peer, and poll B's consumer cursor after Store completion and restart.
Repeat with a present malformed carrier, a wrong key set, a revoked enrollment, and a carrier with one altered signature.
Repeat an exact older legacy fn-r carrier already held at B and an exact kind-4 accepted carrier after key rotation. Send one signed carrier through each NNTP and BP transit caller.
expected: Only the new enrolled, dual-verified carrier publishes a schema-1 kind-4 event containing B's relayed article, exact authored source, selected local snapshot and historical verdict; consumer-project can bind the resulting poll item.
A present malformed or unauthorized carrier refuses without legacy fallback or new Store acceptance; an absent carrier keeps the legacy article path.
An older legacy duplicate remains legacy without a fabricated verdict; an exact historical kind-4 duplicate changes no Store bytes despite later key rotation.
scenarios.execution_scope: ACL2 source projection, local-enrollment selection and event construction plus raw host caller and OpenSSL 3.5.8 raw-key component tests pass. A source-matched saved-image two-Store consumer poll/project, physical crash/reopen, and full owner closure remain open.

scenarios.title: Group names: RFC 5536 grammar and reserved names at creation
steps: Run `operator CONFIG init` with example.test, then with fn.test and Poster, against an absent store.
Initialize with fn.test, then run `group create poster`, `group create Example.a` and `group create fn.poster`.
Run `group create fn..test` and `init` with a name containing a space.
expected: Each init is refused :reserved-group-name with exit 1 and no store directory is created.
poster and Example.a are refused :reserved-group-name with exit 1 and the configuration directory is unchanged; fn.poster is created.
Grammar violations remain usage errors (exit 5) from fn-record-group-namep, distinct from the reserved-name refusal.

scenarios.title: A lost committed suffix beside burned reservations, and the history-class contract
steps: Post two articles; burn a reservation by a known abort and another by process death after reservation.
Delete the newest transaction file and open the store.
Kill or fail the post at each committed-history marker cut and recover.
Compact the store and compare which classes of state each capability removed with the class table.
expected: Burned reservations leave the open admitted and the next post commits at the next sequence.
The open refuses the shortened history with history-short-of-marker, naming the marker and the record count.
Every marker cut recovers; later losses are still refused.
Packing removes transaction files only; no class is removed by a capability its row does not name.
scenarios.execution_scope: Re-pointed by lane log-recovery-2 (PKT-838): the per-file marker, transaction files and their native module (tests/test_native_history_marker.py) went with format 8. On format 9 the committed history is the record log itself (M := D, design 2026-09-27 storage-log section 3.4): a torn or lost tail is zeroed back to the last fenced entry and every log cut recovers to a prefix holding every acknowledged record (tests.test_native_log). The steps and expected lines above are the per-file layout's; their restatement with STO-009 is the registry's.

scenarios.title: Control messages are filed under control.<verb> or refused, never in the groups they name
steps: Initialize a store with fn.test only and POST an article with `Control: cancel <t@example.invalid>` and Newsgroups fn.test; then POST an article with Subject `cmsg cancel <t@example.invalid>` and no Control field.
Create control.cancel and POST a second cancel article naming fn.test; LISTGROUP control.cancel and fn.test.
Repeat the three offers over IHAVE from a configured peer.
expected: The first POST is 441 with the control-not-filed line and ARTICLE by its Message-ID is 430; the cmsg article is 240 and listed in fn.test.
The second cancel is 240, listed in control.cancel, and fn.test's listing is unchanged.
IHAVE answers 437 for the unfiled cancel with the reason in the service log, and 235 for the other two, with the same placement.

scenarios.title: A held bundle is forwarded only to the routed hop; with no route it stays held and no-route is reported
steps: Enrol two boundaries with contact rows and a route from the transit destination to the second boundary; hold a transit bundle for that destination and open the outbound session.
Remove the route and open the session again.
Add the route back and open the session again.

tests/test_native_bp_forward_session_raw.sh (raw SBCL, the shipped fnn-bpnode-forward-session over recording stubs): a hop that resets after SESS_INIT with nothing to send; the normal path; a reset after a durable attempt; the socket shut failing after the close; the connect failing.
expected: The bundle is offered on the routed session to the second boundary and settles status=sent; a session to any other boundary offers nothing.
The log carries `BP forwarding no-route destination=... decision=no-route`, no forwarding attempt (kind 8) is written and the bundle stays held.
The same bundle is forwarded through the routed hop and settles status=sent.

Every forward session that drove ACL2's (:session ... t) open drives its (:session ... nil) close exactly once, so serve rotation (fn-bpnrd-serve-rotation-due-p, no open session) is not blocked by a hop reset; a connect that fails drives neither.

scenarios.title: Open reads the newest verified checkpoint and replays only the suffix; a damaged or absent checkpoint falls back to full replay
steps: On a scale-profile store holding N records run `operator store checkpoint`, then post k more records and open the store (`status`, `recover`).
Corrupt one segment of store-checkpoint.fnsc and open again; remove the file and open again.
Kill the checkpoint publication at each of its five cuts (kill and EIO) and open after each.
expected: status prints open=checkpoint:S suffix=k; the recovered state equals the full-replay state (the keystone fn-sn-recover-from-checkpoint-equals-full-recover); the open wall is bounded by the suffix, not N.
status prints open=full-replay reason=R for the damaged and the absent checkpoint and the recovered state is unchanged.
Each reopen reads the old checkpoint before the rename and the new one at and after it; never a torn file.

scenarios.title: An operator grants and revokes control authority live; a cancel withdraws its target only for its author or a covering authority
steps: On a running owner run `control grant P cancel fn.mod.*` and `control grant Q cancel fn.test`; then grants with a reserved namespace, a malformed principal, the verb newgroup and a malformed pattern.
Stop the owner and run `control list`; restart, revoke P's grant, revoke it again, stop and list.

(Open, C3 served view.) With control.cancel created, an authority's signed cancel of an unsigned fn.mod.a article on two nodes; a reader pinned before it and a fresh reader; an unauthorized cancel; a cross-post outside the grant; the cancel before its target, with a kill between the two arrivals.

(Run, control-c3b/c3c, hbox developer image 5c873f21.) One node, one signing principal P: P's signed T; a reader pinned before; P's signed cancel of T; a fresh reader; P's cancel of a not-yet-arrived L, then L; an unsigned U posted over NNTP and P's cancel of it (no grant); restart.

(control-c3d, two nodes A and B, articles relayed over IHAVE by the test.) P and Q enrolled on both, Q granted cancel over fn.mod.* on B only: P's cancel of P's T1 with a reader on B pinned before it; Q's cancel of an unsigned U in fn.mod.a; P's cancel of T2 before T2 with B killed between the two arrivals; P's S superseding T3; Q's grant revoked on B, then B restarted.
expected: The two grants are accepted; the four are refused by name (reserved-group-name, principal, verb-not-grantable, namespace-pattern) and the owner keeps serving.
`control list` shows both grants after the restart, then only Q's; the second revoke is refused (no-such-grant).

(Open.) The fresh reader answers 430 by Message-ID and 423 `withdrawn` by number and the target is absent from listings; the pinned reader still reads it until it advances; the unauthorized cancel and the cross-post withdraw nothing; the early-cancelled target never appears, across the kill.

(control-c3b, passed natively: planning/evidence/control-c3b-2026-09-25/native-control-filing-a541e90f.log) The fresh reader answers 430 for T and for L; U stays 220; LISTGROUP fn.test lists only U (number 3); after the restart the same; the pinned reader answers 220 for T after the cancel (its pinned view).

(control-c3d, passed natively: planning/evidence/control-c3d-2026-09-25/native-control-filing-e8173157.log) T1 430 on both nodes to a fresh reader, 220 to B's pinned reader; U 430 on B (authority) and 220 on A (no grant); T2 430 on both after the kill and recovery; T3 430 and S 220 on both; after the revoke and restart B still answers 430 for T1, U, T2 and T3 and 220 for S. Open: 423 `withdrawn` by number and HDR :fn-control on the served path.

scenarios.title: A retry resolved as already stored after a crash before its marker is covered without a later commit; after migration a missing marker is damage
steps: Post one article; post a second with the process killed (or EIO) at each committed-history marker cut, through `store ROOT post` and through the served owner.
Retry the second submission; commit nothing else; delete the newest transaction file; open twice.

On a store without a marker (or one behind its history) run `operator store upgrade-profile --history-marker required`, with and without a kill or EIO at each marker and profile cut; then delete the marker, and separately the newest transaction file, and open.
expected: The record is durable at every marker cut; the retry's open writes the marker of the reconstructed count before answering, and the retry is answered as already stored with no new transaction.
Both opens refuse with history-short-of-marker naming the marker and the record count (exit 4).

Each interrupted migration reopens unmarked or required, and required only over the covering marker; after migration status prints history-marker=required, a deleted marker is marker-missing (exit 4), a lost newest file is history-short-of-marker, a downgrade is refused by name, and init refuses required.
scenarios.execution_scope: Re-pointed by lane log-recovery-2 (PKT-838): the per-file marker, transaction files and their native module (tests/test_native_history_required.py) went with format 8. On format 9 the committed history is the record log itself (M := D, design 2026-09-27 storage-log section 3.4): a torn or lost tail is zeroed back to the last fenced entry and every log cut recovers to a prefix holding every acknowledged record (tests.test_native_log). The steps and expected lines above are the per-file layout's; their restatement with STO-009 is the registry's.

scenarios.title: status, pins, obligations and peer list answer from the running owner in the words the offline command prints
steps: Start `operator CONFIG run`; post articles; run `operator CONFIG status`, `pins`, `obligations`, `peer list`, and `status --watch 1` for a few seconds.
While a POST burst runs against the owner, run `status` repeatedly and time each answer.
Stop the owner cleanly and run the same four commands offline.
expected: Each answers 0 from the owner (no `store is already locked`) with the report fn-nls-live-report renders; --watch repeats it.
Each status answers within its budget and every POST of the burst is accepted as without status.

The offline words equal the owner's last words for the same committed state (fn-nls-live-report-is-the-offline-report); only the open= line, which names each process's own open, and connection lines may differ.

scenarios.title: Reclaim under released-by-all-holders removes exactly the unheld payloads, and a reclaimed Message-ID stays a duplicate
steps: On a store of N=5,000 articles in one group, run `admin retention set released-by-all-holders`; hold article 100 by a reader pin, articles above 2,000 by a consumer cursor at 2,000, and articles 3,000 to 3,100 by an undelivered feed to a live peer.
Run `store reclaim --dry-run`, then `store reclaim`; record the disk use of the store before and after.
Re-post the Message-ID of a reclaimed article with its original bytes, and with changed bytes; ARTICLE it by Message-ID and by number; STAT and ARTICLE a held one.
Kill `store reclaim` at each cut of its program (SIGKILL and EIO) and reopen after each.

Inspect the rewritten event through the current FN-RCL2 codec: preserve the typed relay-v1 commitment and original byte-content commitment; change the magic to the retired RCL1 value and truncate below 145 bytes to confirm neither is recognized.
expected: The dry run names every article with its verdict; exactly articles 1 to 2,000 except 100 are reclaimable, and 100 is held-reader-pin, 2,001 to 5,000 held-consumer-cursor.
After the run the same numbers are tombstones (verified by number), the others are byte-identical, and disk use falls by the reclaimed payload octets less the tombstones.
The original bytes are refused as a duplicate, the changed bytes as a conflict; ARTICLE answers 430 and 423 article reclaimed; the held article is served unchanged.
Every reopen replays to a state whose Message-IDs, numbers and group bindings equal the state before; each article is either its original payload or its tombstone.

The host per-event rewriter retains fn-asj-subject of the original payload exactly; permitted Path/Xref variants share that commitment. This is commitment preservation, not digest injectivity or a claim that the duplicate decision already uses it.

scenarios.title: A stock third-party reader (tin) posts, replies and cancels its own post: its supplied Path is accepted and prefixed
steps: Start a developer-image node with a posting login; point tin 2.6.2 (NNTP-only) at it through the wire logger.
Post a new article from tin, reply to it, and cancel the new post with tin's cancel command.
Resend one POST's exact octets; resend it with a changed Path.
expected: Each tin POST is answered 240; ARTICLE shows `Path: IDENTITY!not-for-mail` (the node's identity prefixed to tin's Path) and no other Path.
The cancel is filed under the control rules in force (C1).
The exact resend is `441 posting failed; this article is already stored here`; the changed Path is `441 posting failed; a different article with this Message-ID is stored here`.

scenarios.title: A bound login posts only as its bound principal under the bound-logins policy; an unbound login and a policy-off node post as before
steps: Enrol logins ember and guest with posting and hybrid keys; `principal bind ember EMBER-HEX`; restart; `policy set posting-policy bound-logins`.
As ember, POST an article signed with ember's key, one signed with guest's key, and one unsigned.
As guest (unbound), POST an unsigned article; then `policy set posting-policy open` and repeat ember's guest-signed and unsigned POSTs.
expected: `principal list` prints signing=EMBER-HEX for ember only.

240 with HDR :fn-verified naming ember's principal; `441 posting failed; the login is not bound to this signing principal`; `441 posting failed; this login posts only articles signed by its bound principal`. The service log names login=ember for each.
240 for guest; with the policy open, 240 for both of ember's articles (the guest-signed one verified for guest's principal).

scenarios.title: RETIRED (D34): an operator raises max-credentials and max-config-generations on a format-8 store and a credential file above the pre-D27 cap loads
steps: Copy a format-8 store; run `operator CONFIG store upgrade-profile --max-credentials 200 --max-config-generations 9000`, then `status`.
Write an auth.toml of 129 credentials with `principal set-password` and start the owner.
Run `store upgrade-profile --max-credentials 150` on the upgraded store.
expected: The upgrade exits 0; status prints max-credentials=200 and max-config-generations=9000.
The 129th login is accepted and the owner starts (the pre-D27 cap was 128); under a profile of 128 the 129th set-password is refused too-many-credentials.
The shrink is refused (exit 1) naming max-credentials.
scenarios.retirement_note: D34 removed store upgrade-profile; raising a field is now store export then store import --FIELD N (SCN-133).

scenarios.title: a carrying boundary holds articles only within its budget, and a refused present carrier is named by its class
steps: Relay R adds peer A with no carried list, then `peer carries A HEX` and `peer budget A OCTETS 1`; A posts two signed articles by a principal R never enrolled.
Without `peer budget`, A's signed article reaches R.
From A's address, offer R by IHAVE an article whose FN-Authorship items name suite 2, and one by a principal R never enrolled and does not carry.
expected: R stores the first with a carried verdict and refuses the second with detail=carried-count-exhausted.
R refuses it with detail=carried-budget-unset.
R answers 437 to each, logging detail=unsupported-profile and detail=no-local-binding.

scenarios.title: XPAT is listed, joins its pattern arguments, ORs comma alternatives and matches case-sensitively on the served node
steps: CAPABILITIES on a served connection.
In a group holding an article with Subject `probe root`: XPAT Subject 1-9 *root*, *Root*, *zzz*,*root*, *zzz* *root*, probe root.
Search the group from the web reader with the wildmat *root*.
expected: The capability block lists XPAT.
221 with the article's line for *root*, *zzz*,*root* and probe root; 221 with an empty list for *Root* and *zzz* *root*.
The web page names the XPAT command it sent, carrying the wildmat as typed, and lists the article.
scenarios.note: assurance-triage 2026-09-26: returned to specified: the served-node steps were not run (planning/evidence/reader-surface-2026-09-25.md "Native: NOT RUN (blocked)"); only the fake-node tests.test_fn_web ReaderSearchTests and the ACL2 book ran.

scenarios.title: A store written by an image before the u64 record codec opens under the new image with the same records and bytes; a u64 charge commits as schema 2
steps: With the previous image, init a store and post two articles; hash every file.
Open it with the new image (recover, status) and hash every file again.
With the new image post an article with charge 2^40 and recover.
expected: The new image recovers the same transaction and article counts; every file hash is unchanged by the open.
The u64 charge commits (schema-2 record) and recovers; the previous image refuses the store's new record fail-closed by its version octet.
scenarios.note: assurance-triage 2026-09-26: returned to specified: the only recorded native run (planning/evidence/bounds-p6-2026-09-25.md, the u64 charge) refused the 2^40 charge ("charge must be a positive uint32") and wrote no schema-2 record, the opposite of the expected result; no test or script is committed.

scenarios.title: The checkpoint open is cheaper than full replay and an automatic publication does not hold served commands
