steps: On scale-profile stores of N = 1000 and N = 4096 records (2 KiB articles), time `status` and the owner's start to LISTENING with no checkpoint and from `operator store checkpoint`'s file, on the image before and after the change.
Start the owner on the N = 4096 store whose checkpoint is at S = 2048 (due at its first tick) and send STAT in a loop while it publishes S = 4096.
expected: The open from the checkpoint takes less wall time than the full replay on the same image, the file is smaller than before, and both opens serve the same state (fn-sco-store-open-of-extended-capture).
No STAT waits for the publication: the largest STAT latency during it stays at the served-command scale, not the publication's seconds.
scenarios.note: assurance-triage 2026-09-26: returned to specified: no committed harness or log, and the recorded measurements (planning/evidence/checkpoint-cost-2026-09-25.md) show owner start from a checkpoint slower than full replay (1.36 vs 1.10 s; 8.94 vs 7.28 s) and status at N=4096 about equal (7.72 vs 7.77 s), not the expected result.

scenarios.title: A principal's key succession and revocation reach two peering nodes as signed statements and act only where verified
steps: Enrol P at nodes A and B; grant P the verb keys over fn.keys at both.
P posts a succession statement signed by the old key with a PoP by the new key; it reaches B by transit.
P posts an article under the old key; then one under the new key.
A carried copy of a succession for another principal reaches B.
P posts a revocation; an article P signed before it is delivered to B by IHAVE after it.
Kill the owner after the statement's kind-4 commit (FN_NATIVE_KEY_STATEMENT_FAULT=statement-committed:kill) and restart it.
expected: Each node enrols the new keys at its next generation (fn-ks-execute) and logs key-statement enrol-successor committed.
The old-key article is refused 437/441 local-enrollment; the new-key article is verified at the new generation.
The carried statement declines (key-statement declined carried) and changes no keyring.
The late article is stored as revoked HEX keyring G at B; a served POST of it is refused 441 local-enrollment; articles stored before stay verified.
At the cut the keyring is unchanged; the restart logs key-statement enrol-successor committed at-open and the new keys are current; a second restart changes nothing.

scenarios.title: Two nodes that share no key peer by invitation; tampered, replayed, foreign and repeated documents are refused, and a crash between consumption and enrolment enrols once
steps: On A and B run `peer genesis` over fresh key directories; start both owners.
A: `peer invite nodeB fn.* HOST PORT a.example KEYS OUT`; B: `peer accept OUT KEYS b.example - ACC`; A: `peer confirm ACC`.
A: confirm ACC again; B: accept the invitation again; A: confirm a tampered ACC, an acceptance of another invitation, and an acceptance of the consumed nonce by another principal.
On a developer image, A2: invite, B: accept, A2: confirm with FN_PEER_TEST_STOP_AFTER_CONSUME set; restart A2 and confirm again, then once more.
expected: Each verb exits 0; A's key history lists B's principal and B's lists A's.

The second confirm and the second accept are refused (1) as already-confirmed and already-enrolled; the tampered acceptance is refused unverified; the foreign one another-invitation; the replayed nonce invitation-consumed.
A2 dies after the consuming record; after restart the confirm exits 0 and enrols B once; the next confirm is refused already-confirmed.

scenarios.title: a node behind NAT pulls from a second fn node and from INN by NEWNEWS, and a crash mid-round skips no id
steps: B (behind NAT: no peer record for B anywhere, only B dials) adds peer A (inbound fn.*, outbound none) and `peer pull A 2`; A holds two articles in fn.test; a recording proxy in front of A logs every command B sends.
A third article is held at A; the proxy withholds B's ARTICLE for it, so B's round is frozen after NEWNEWS and a local 335; B is killed (SIGKILL) there and restarted.
B adds INN 2.7.4's nnrpd (a private innd and nnrpd on hbox) as a peer with `peer pull INN 2`; INN holds an article in fn.test, injected into innd by IHAVE.
expected: B's next round lists both, stores both (235), and its FNPL cursor advances once; the next round answers 435 or lists nothing.
After restart B's first NEWNEWS names the same instant as the killed round's, and the third article is stored.
B stores INN's article (235) and its cursor for INN advances.

scenarios.title: A request above the receiving node's Transfer MRU is fragmented, reassembled once and delivered once
steps: Serve the receiver with a Transfer MRU below the request bundle's length.
Send the request with `bp-service run`.
expected: The sender logs `BP fragmenting` with more than one fragment, each at most the peer's MRU, and every further fragment's transfer is accepted.
The receiver publishes the fragment family once and hands the reassembled request to the application once: one article in its Store.

scenarios.title: Two strangers become peers with one confirm, and a declined key statement stays declined across a restart that adds the grant
steps: A and B run `peer genesis`; A: `peer invite nodeB fn.* HOST PORT a.example KEYS INV`; B: `peer accept INV KEYS b.example - ACC`; A: `peer confirm ACC INV`; A: `peer list`.
A: `peer confirm ACC INV-OTHER` with another invitation A issued; A2 with FN_PEER_TEST_STOP_AFTER_CONSUME: confirm, restart, `peer list`, confirm again.
Node D: enrol P, POST a succession statement with no `keys` grant; `control grant P keys fn.keys` live; restart D twice.
expected: The confirm exits 0 and `peer list` shows nodeB with auth principal B.
Another invitation is refused another-invitation and configures nothing; after the stop A2 already lists nodeB2, and the retry enrols once.

The statement logs `key-statement declined no-grant`; after each restart the log adds `key-statement declined ... at-open` and the key history is unchanged (the pre-packet image instead logs `enrol-successor committed at-open`).

scenarios.title: a POST whose reply was lost, then withdrawn by an authorized cancel, is settled by re-sending the same article: already stored, no new Message-ID, no new number
steps: A developer node with fn.test and control.cancel; the owner runs with FN_NATIVE_POST_FAULT=finish-durable:kill. fn_client posts with --draft and the owner dies after the commit is durable, before the reply (exit 3, uncertain); fn_web posts through its outbox under the same cut.
The owner restarts; both targets answer 220. A principal granted cancel over fn.test files a signed cancel of each target.
A fresh reader asks ARTICLE <target> for both; fn_client show <target>.
fn_client reconcile DRAFT and fn_web POST /reconcile re-send the exact stored lines; then reconcile again.
On a protected node the poster's login loses posting permission after a lost reply; fn_client reconcile.
expected: Both lookups answer 430 withdrawn; show exits 1 and says the answer is not evidence about acceptance.

Both reconciliations draw 441 posting failed; this article is already stored here and settle accepted (already-stored); the transaction files and GROUP fn.test are unchanged; the draft and outbox keep the original outcome uncertain beside the reconciliation.
The authorization case answers 440 and settles unresolved (exit 4); the article is still served (220) and nothing is stored.

scenarios.title: One authored article keeps one identity through every route, and the node shows the table
steps: Two developer-image nodes A and B, A feeding B, each with a path identity
POST each corpus element to A, retry it at a later second, and POST it with one authored byte changed
Post three elements again through the operator route; author a signed article through hybrid-author and POST a dual-signature carrier
Await each accepted article at B and re-offer it by IHAVE
SIGKILL and reopen A; reread every article and retry four elements
Stop both nodes and read every record with store inspect
On one node: target then cancel with a pinned reader, cancel then target, a Supersedes; SIGKILL and reopen
expected: Xref refused; every other element 240; a retry 441 already stored; a changed byte 441 a different article; a legacy post without Message-ID is a new article on retry
The operator route answers DUPLICATE and adds no article; the supplied Path tail is kept behind A's identity; every source and the carrier are stored verbatim after the injected block
B stores A's octets with its identity and an empty diagnostic spliced into Path; the re-offer is 435; numbers and octets are unchanged across reopen; store inspect equals the served octets
Both cancel orders withdraw their targets from every fresh view, live and after replay; the pinned reader keeps 220; the superseding article stays visible
hybrid-author's resend of the same signed carrier is DUPLICATE, exit 0; the same source signed afresh (hedged ML-DSA-65) or changed is REFUSED, exit 1; no article is added

scenarios.title: A person reads a conversation across a withdrawn message, searches a stated window, and resends an uncertain post only on request
steps: On a scratch developer-image node, post a root, a signed reply and a further reply; withdraw the signed reply with its author's signed cancel.

Open the group, the withdrawn number, the conversation of the last reply, and a search of the group in the web reader; reply with a double-click, go Back and press Post again; post while the node is unreachable, restart the client, and press Re-send this same article to settle it.
expected: The group window lists the withdrawn number with the node's 423 withdrawn; the conversation lists the withdrawn reply with the node's 430 withdrawn and shows the root and the last reply from the node's XPAT References answer.

The search page names the node's XPAT command and window; the article page shows claimed From, carriers, the node's historical verdict (HDR :fn-verified), the node's current enrollment of that verdict's principal (HDR :fn-enrollment: active, retired, revoked, unenrolled or a named none) and the reader's own independent verification with the reader's own keyring (verified here, failed here with the reason, or not performed with why), separately.

Back after posting shows that the form was already posted and sends nothing; after restart the intent is uncertain and nothing is sent until the button; the reconciliation answer is recorded beside the unchanged original (NNT-019).
scenarios.note: Retired 2026-09-28 (lane web-native-2) with tools/fn_web.py and tools/fn_reader.py: the web page is the node's own face (WEB-005). This scenario ran against the Python reader; its record stays as history.

scenarios.title: Two sleeping consumers exchange a signed report and reply through one node across every ownership cut
steps: A authors signed report R through its outbox and sleeps.
B wakes three times, dying inside its transaction, after its commit, and while the owner loses its ack reply; then dies after settling the ack before posting Q; then the owner loses Q's POST reply.
B wakes and settles Q; A wakes after Q is durable; a third author reuses R's operation id with a different source; both consumers wake.
expected: B's database holds nothing after the in-transaction death and exactly one transition and one outbox Q after the commit; fn's position moves only with the ack and the lost ack is settled by position.
Q is stored once and settled by the owner of that fact; A records exactly one reply transition; the reused operation id is conflict evidence at both consumers with no second transition or reply.

scenarios.title: A signed report crosses four native fn nodes and two dtn7-rs relays with outages and restarts; its receipt settles before the receiver's consumer wakes; the reply returns
steps: A holds a signed report with a durable obligation; B's consumer is registered and asleep.
A requests it toward B through fn relay X (small Transfer MRU: fragmented, reassembled at X), dtn7 relays r1 and r2, and fn relay Y, with links down and every node restarted at least once.
B takes custody, delivers to its Store and queues the application receipt; the receipt crosses its own outage back to A.
B's consumer wakes, verifies, acknowledges and replies; the reply crosses back; A's consumer wakes and consumes it.
expected: A answers receipt-accepted and its obligation is receipted with pinned=no before B's consumer polls.
B's poll returns the report with its authored source; the reply is delivered at A and A's receipt releases B's pin.
Every boundary names its identities (work, attempt, Message-ID, authored-source digest, bundle, attempts, receipt).
scenarios.note: Passes on the lane image aa0f6c16 (not deployed; loopback on hbox): the signed report and the signed reply, all seven steps, 153.9 s (native-aa0f6c16/signed-r2, report.json 55580c3b36fb66dd...), and the unsigned control, all seven steps (unsigned-r2, 25bcafe453675d7e...). Relays listen per boundary, so the driver turns a relay's listener and restarts the node whose receipt is owed (PKT-291). planning/evidence/mission-signed-2-2026-09-26.md.

scenarios.title: A node pulls over TLS as its own principal; a wrong principal and a clear-transport credential are refused, and the cut campaign holds over TLS
steps: A: store with STARTTLS, `[auth] required = true, protected_only = true`, `principal set-password nodeB`; two articles posted with `operator post`. B: `peer add A a.pull.example.invalid 127.0.0.1 PORT fn.* fn.* source-address 127.0.0.9 PROFILE false false starttls localhost A-CERT`, `peer pull A 2`, PROFILE = FNAUTH1 nodeB and its password; a recording proxy in front of A.
The same with PROFILE naming a login A does not hold.
The same with no security arguments (a clear transport) and the permission false.
Packet 5's campaign over the TLS transport: FN_PULL_TEST_KILL=CUT:N at before-write, after-write and after-fsync of appends 1 and 2, restart without the fault.
The TLS pull with its local profile changed to mode 0644 before B starts.
expected: Both articles stored once at B; B logs `pull peer=A round=done cursor=advanced transport=tls`; the proxy's first plaintext command is STARTTLS and it sees no AUTHINFO, DATE, NEWNEWS or ARTICLE in the clear.
B logs `round=failed cursor=held at=preamble` for every round, stores nothing, and its FNPL journal stays at the first-instant record.
B logs `round=failed cursor=held refused=clear-credential` for every round and the proxy accepts no connection.
At every cut every article is stored exactly once at B and a later round logs `cursor=advanced transport=tls`.

B names the ACL2 credential outcome, holds its cursor with refused=profile, stays live and the recording proxy accepts no connection; native credential case requires matching new source/image evidence.

scenarios.title: A family of more fragments than the old 64-fragment ceiling, interrupted by a receiver kill, reassembles once and is delivered once
steps: Raise the receiving node's profile to 128 held rows (`bp-node profile JOURNAL NODE 128 16777216`); a write that lowers it again is refused (exit 1).
Author one request ADU and cut it into 70 fragments (fn-bpf-cut).
Serve the receiver continuously; send 35 fragments, highest offset first; kill the receiver with SIGKILL.
Restart the receiver on the same journal and send the other 35, offset zero last.
expected: Before the kill no family is published and the Store holds no article.
After the restart the receiver logs `BP fragment family durable` once and `BP application handoff durable` once, and the Store holds one article.

scenarios.title: `store reclaim` returns released payload octets and inodes to the file system, survives a cut at every step, and a reclaimed article never comes back
steps: Build a store of N articles in one group (one pack: N up to about 4,000), keep-forever: run `store reclaim`.
`retention set release-after 1`: `store reclaim --dry-run`. `retention set released-by-all-holders`: `store reclaim --dry-run`, `store compact`.
On a copy per cut, stop or kill `store reclaim` at every publication, selection and retirement cut and kill and EIO at each reclaim-* cut; reopen with `status`, rerun `store reclaim`.
Run `store reclaim`; record files, octets and du before and after, and `status` headroom; rerun it.
Serve: GROUP, ARTICLE by Message-ID and number, OVER, STAT, NEWNEWS; re-POST a reclaimed article's original bytes.
On a store refused for history headroom, run `store compact` and `store reclaim`.

PKT-857 (tests/test_native_replay_determinism.py test f): `retention set released-by-all-holders` on a copy of the mixed store; `store reclaim` on copy A; copy the one new config/ file A published into copy B and run `store reclaim --recorded` on B; run `store reclaim --recorded` on copy C, which has no recorded instant.
expected: keep-forever writes nothing (reclaimed=0, exit 0).
release-after 1 reclaims nothing (too recent); the dry run names every article and writes nothing.
Every reopen exits 0 and every rerun exits 0 with the clean run's selected pack bytes.
Files and octets fall by the old generation; bytes-used falls by the freed octets; a rerun reclaims 0.
GROUP is unchanged; ARTICLE answers 430 and 423 article reclaimed; OVER 423; NEWNEWS lists no reclaimed article; the re-POST is 441 (a duplicate).
Both refuse by name (temporary-space), exit 1, nothing written: the maintenance reservation finding (PKT-169).

A's report names its instant record (instant-record=NAME) and it is the one new config/ file; B's report equals A's (reclaimed, freed octets, the Message-IDs) and B's `store digest` equals A's; C is refused by name (no-recorded-instant) and its digest is the pre-reclaim store's.

scenarios.title: Operator health names each of its states on a scratch node, with its own line and exit code
steps: Initialize a scratch node with the development profile and run `health` offline.
Upgrade the profile, start the owner, add an outbound peer on a closed port and post into its groups; run `health`.
Raise [alerts] headroom_min_percent to 100; run `health`.
Undertake a BP forwarding obligation with no bp-route; run `health`; add a route; run `health`.
Remove the control socket of a running owner; run `health`.
expected: Each run prints eight lines in the fixed order and exits with the code of the first held state: 22 unqualified-profile, 26 unavailable-peer, 23 space-pressure, 24 no-route then 27 receipt-debt, 20 fenced (store-held); offline the feed states are unobserved, never clear.

scenarios.title: the served POST charges an article its own worst case before a transaction ID is reserved: an article past the remaining history is refused 441 and the store reopens, where the fixed-figure gate accepted it and left the store unopenable
steps: On hbox, a developer store initialised with T 4, H 250 000, R 196 608, A 150 000, G 8 (fn.test), served by `operator run` on loopback.
POST a 148 112-octet article, then a second one of the same size (planning/evidence/width-producers-2-nntp-post.py).
Stop the node; `store recover` and `store status`.
The same on the image before the article gate (bbf52159).
expected: The first POST answers 240; the second 441 posting failed; the store is full: no capacity for this article (unaffordable); the node's operator can raise it (the owner's :unaffordable from fn-sbud-article-budget-for), with one transaction file of 148 613 octets.
The reopen succeeds (recovered transactions=1, exit 0).
Before the gate both POSTs answer 240, 297 226 record octets are committed past H, and every reopen refuses: transaction recovery input exceeds configured bound (exit 4).

scenarios.title: The operator walk: one installed fn from nothing to a recovered node on two scratch nodes
steps: Install the production image with packaging/install-native.sh into a scratch prefix; every later command is PREFIX/bin/fn.

Write a small-community fn.toml with `mission`; ask status, health and run before init; init with a profile word, then init; init again; show the port; set the path identity; status and health offline.
Enrol a login; peer two nodes; start both; status live; post; the peer's log names the fed article; health live; post over the article bound.
Give a node a streaming peer that answers MODE STREAM with 501, and one that answers another refusal; post to each.

Stop, back up the node folder (docs/operator.md section 9), start, post two more, stop; restore the backup on a copy with rewritten paths; recover, status, run; post the backup's article and a later one.
SIGKILL the owner; status, recover, run, health, status.
expected: Before init: refused NO-STORE exit 1 with the init line, never a fault (specs/host.md "CLI exit codes", HST-009); init with a profile word under a mission is usage 5 (MISSION-FIXES-PROFILE) and writes no store; init again is refused STORE-EXISTS; health of a node not running is exit 18 (not-running).

The 501 peer receives MODE STREAM once and is fed with IHAVE on the same connection, the owner logging mode-stream-unsupported once and health exit 0 (fn-fc-mode-stream-unsupported-falls-back-to-ihave); the peer answering any other refusal receives MODE STREAM once, is stopped by name (reason=mode-stream-refused) and not dialled again for new work, health exit 26 unavailable-peer (fn-fc-mode-stream-refusal-stops-the-dial).

The restored copy recovers and serves the backup's state: the backup's article is a DUPLICATE, a later one is ACCEPTED; after the SIGKILL the control socket file stays, status and recover exit 0 and the restarted owner's health is 0.
scenarios.execution_scope: Native, through the installed launcher on scratch loopback nodes (stores on durable local storage, FN_TEST_DURABLE_TMP), one host; D34 retired the walk's upgrade rehearsal and rollback-check (one store format, a new release is a fresh install): the backup step is the operator guide's copy of the stopped node folder. The walk script planning/evidence/operator-walk-2026-09-26/walk.sh is the 2026-09-26 record, superseded by the module.

scenarios.title: A store filled to its history bound keeps the room for a release, compacts and reclaims on the disk's free space, refuses a pack the disk cannot hold by name, and admits again after the reclaim
steps: Init a store with max_history_octets 300,000 and POST 1 KiB articles until the first refusal; `retention set released-by-all-holders`; read `status`.
On a copy, with the developer image's observed free space capped at 1,000 octets (FN_NATIVE_DISK_FREE), run `store compact`.
Run `store compact` on the store; on a copy, with the same cap, run `store reclaim`.
Run `store reclaim`; read `status`; POST another article.
expected: The refused POST is 441 (no capacity); `status` shows `maintenance-reserve octets=4096 transactions=1 held` at the bound.
`compaction refused: temporary-space`, exit 1, the copy's files unchanged.
`store compact` exits 0 on the full store; the capped `store reclaim` is refused temporary-space, exit 1, unchanged.
`store reclaim` exits 0 and frees octets on disk and in bytes-used; the reservation is held; the next POST is 240.

scenarios.title: The signed mission: A's hybrid-signed report crosses four fn nodes and two dtn7-rs relays to B, B's signed reply comes back, every refusal names its reason, and a relay takes no custody from a channel its policy refused
steps: A's author signs the report (Ed25519 + ML-DSA-65) and hybrid-author stores its portable carrier; both authors are enrolled at A and B through hybrid-enroll.
The SCN-066 sequence runs with the signed report: fragmentation at X, the relays each listening on the boundary of the neighbour that sends toward them, restarts of all four nodes.
B verifies the delivered copy with hybrid-verify-source, consumes it and returns a signed reply the same way.
The ambiguous-peer case: X's two boundaries on one listener; A's transfer to X.
expected: B answers request-accepted for the signed report and A for the signed reply; both receipts release their pins (pinned=no); all seven steps hold.
Every refused delivered request prints `BP node delivery refused result=... reason=...` with ACL2's reason.

scenarios.title: A pinned reader's payload handle reads the same octets after later commits, and an opened store's arena is its history's payloads in order
steps: Seal three payloads into a live local arena (a list, the octet buffer's contents, the empty payload) and read every handle back; seal 3,000 octets three times through the byte array's doubling and the handle arrays' growth.
Read handle 1 before and after a later seal, and after a sequence of seals; read the handle at the count after a seal.
Build a two-record history, seal a third record's payload as a commit would, and seal every record's payload from the empty arena as an open would.
expected: Every handle reads back the payload sealed under it; the count is the number of seals; a clear empties the arena.
Handle 1 is unchanged by every later seal; the handle at the old count is the new payload; a negative handle or a handle at the count is not covered and reads otherwise (the must-fail witnesses).

The arena after the commit's seal is the appended history's payloads; the arena after the open's seals equals the history's payloads; an arena with the payloads in the wrong order or one payload missing does not satisfy the relation.

scenarios.title: A 10 MiB article carried by BP through 4 KiB fragments, under a node profile that admits it, is reassembled once and handed to the Store once
steps: Raise the receiving node's profile (`bp-node profile JOURNAL NODE ROWS OCTETS ADU BUNDLE`) to at least 2,623 held rows, 16 MiB of held octets and an ADU of at least 10,486,094 octets, and the Store profile's max-article-octets to at least 10 MiB.
Author one 10 MiB request ADU and send it through a route whose Transfer MRU is 4 KiB, so the sender cuts it into fragments (RFC 9171 5.8).
Kill the receiver with SIGKILL halfway through the family, restart it on the same journal, and send the rest.
expected: The receiver publishes one kind-18 family, logs `BP application handoff durable disposition=request-accepted` once, and the Store holds one article whose bytes are the ADU. Under the development-base Store (32,768-octet articles) the Store refuses the article as oversize and the handoff is reported refused (PKT-630 (7), PRF-224): the harness raises the Store profile (--max-article-octets 11534336 --max-record-octets 33554432 --max-history-octets 268435456).

Arrivals no longer block it (PRF-136, bp-lifecycle-5): a bp-node serve session costs about 60 ms at 64 to 256 held rows (3.7 to 15.9 s before) and the first 1,311 fragments arrive in 90 s. Blocked now by the open: a journal of 1,311 held rows opens in 51.9 s (three re-encodings per row, an unverified bundle decode, a quadratic held-octet sum), so the restarted receiver misses the harness's waits in the second half. PKT-308. 2026-09-27 (bp-fragments-10mib): the reopen and the family pass; with the Store and the neighbour's inbound bound raised the delivery is refused by FNRJ, whose request-ADU :blob is 131,072 octets (PKT-646, open), and reported `BP application handoff refused disposition=request-refused (kind 7 durable)`. Reassembly and handoff 280.3 s -> 117.2 s with the table-driven CRC-16 (PRF-225). 2026-09-27 (bp-fragments-10mib-4): PKT-646 closed; accepted, `disposition=request-accepted`, and the Store's own open reads one article byte-equal to the authored one (`store PATH status`, `store PATH inspect`), on the developer and production images at be7e5cb17 (tests.test_bp_fragment_node_native).

2026-09-30 current-source regression: E739 produced no durable family at the final fragment because the host used the 1 MiB received-wire budget for the whole internal image. The corrected host reads max-held-octets for reassembly. Original 10 MiB input, 4 KiB fragments, 16 MiB held budget, 11 MiB ADU budget and 1 MiB received-wire budget remain unchanged. Matching current native result is pending; historical be7e5cb17 validation is not transferred.

steps: On a live local buffer, plan a ground checkpoint-shaped value at segment sizes 7 (eight frames), 0 and 1000 (one frame), 56 and 55 (a chunk boundary at the end), and the empty value; compare the plan's octets with fn-scc-file-octets, the buffer with fn-scc-encode, and read the segments back with fn-scc-decode-segments; plan a value the codec refuses.

On hbox, copies of the wave-d stores (N = 1,000 x 32 KiB, N = 10,000 x 2 KiB, N = 10,000 x 32 KiB; planning/evidence/rep-wave-d-2026-09-25.md section 1) under the same 40G scope: `store checkpoint` timed with GNU time -v (the baseline's conditions), then the owner opened from the checkpoint to its LISTENING line with VmRSS and VmHWM read from /proc.

For REP-011 (the record's payload as an arena handle), the same harness rows the wave-d baseline has (live heap after collection, allocation per POST, peak residency, reopen, checkpoint, OVER, ARTICLE) at N = 1,000 and N = 10,000 x 2 KiB and x 32 KiB, once the freeze lands under PKT-293's answer.

The N = 10,000 x 32 KiB publication completes inside the 40G scope where the baseline died by heap exhaustion at 32,000 MB after 253 s; the two smaller points publish files of the same octets as before; the numbers are in the record's table.

scenarios.title: The state checkpoint is read from the octet buffer: the node reopens from the N = 10,000 x 32 KiB checkpoint it published, and a file past the profile's bounds is refused by name
steps: On a live local buffer, plan the ground checkpoint-shaped value at segment sizes 7, 0, 1000, 56 and 55 and decode each plan back with fn-sccr-decode-plan; compare with fn-scc-decode-segments over the frames' octets; corrupt the buffer (a flipped octet) and the plan (a dropped frame, a broken first header, frames sealed under the wrong sequence, a non-contiguous plan, a short header) and compare the verdicts; run the index machine against the list machine on the program and its every suffix; admit a header at, one short of, and past the segment bound and the file bound.

tests.test_native_state_checkpoint on the image built from the lane's tree: a corrupt checkpoint falls back to full replay (reason=corrupt), a checkpoint whose first segment claims a length past the profile's segment bound is refused by name (reason=checkpoint-exceeds-bound) and the journal replays, the checkpoint open equals the full replay, and the host's source calls the reader's subjects.

scenarios.title: A consumer that dies between fn's acceptance and its own record never records the operation refused, resends only its saved artifact, and consumes only reports it verified itself

On copies, stop and kill the next `operator store compact` after the first and second retirement unlink (pack-retire-unlink 1, 2) and at the retirement directory barrier; status; recover; `checkpoint pack-retire`; recover; compact again.

From the 20,000-record chain fixture built once (planning/evidence/pack-chain-open-2026-09-26/chain_fixture.py build: probe 20000 article on tmpfs, the served view of every article by number, eight by Message-ID and HDR Subject, the retention listing, then `operator store compact`; kept at /tank/fn/scratch/fixtures/chain-20000 with its SHA256SUMS), a copy is recovered, served (the owner's startup deadline is the class's served_timeout), posted to once, served again and compacted again (FN_P5_FIXTURE).

scenarios.title: The served commit's barrier cost measured on ZFS and tmpfs, and the N = 10,000 POST curve profiled from inside the image without a polling thread
steps: On hbox, the developer image of the revision under test in /tank/fn/scratch/publish-program/native-REV/tree: `store STORE probe 100` under `strace -f -c` on tmpfs and on the pool (syncs.sh), then `probe N` at N = 1,000 and 10,000 on /dev/shm and on /tank/fn/scratch/publish-program timed with /usr/bin/time, then 100 POSTs of 2 KiB on one connection to `operator run` on each (measure.sh, post.py); every row names the pool's used/free and the box load.

10,000 POSTs of 2 KiB over one connection to an owner started by the launcher's own sbcl line with prof-owner.lisp loaded before ACL2's restart (sb-sprof :cpu, every thread, no poll of the file system); every POST timed, a POST over --timeout seconds treated as a stall (thread states, a 10 s strace, SIGUSR1 to the profiler); at the end SIGUSR1 writes the flat and graph reports (post_n.py).
expected: The sync-family counts per commit are the same on both file systems: fsync 7, rename 2, link 1, unlink 1 (plus the reopen's).

The per-commit wall on the pool is the barrier count times the pool's ZIL commit latency (hundreds of ms under load), on tmpfs about 1 ms; the POST median and p95 on the pool are of the same order as the probe's commit.
No POST stalls; the per-POST median grows linearly with N (fn-own-refresh's group-index rebuild, PKT-324 item 1); the profile's dominant term is named, and no term is the profiler's own.

scenarios.title: An operator after a crash: a SIGKILLed owner's socket does not lock out the offline control verbs, and health during a slow start says starting; every refusal names its reason on the wire, and an old client's plain request still reads the plain reply
steps: Start an owner with a configured control socket; SIGKILL it; `operator CONFIG control list`; start the owner again and stop it.
Start a developer owner with FN_NATIVE_OWNER_TEST_PAUSE_BEFORE_LISTEN (the store recovered and locked, no socket yet); `operator CONFIG health`; SIGTERM the owner.

With an owner running: `operator CONFIG post` an article whose From has no address, and one naming a newsgroup the node does not serve; post a well-formed one; `operator CONFIG control revoke` a grant that does not exist.
With an owner running: send a plain kind-3 FNCT admin frame (`control grant`), as every client before the reasoned kinds does, and read the reply; then `control revoke` the grant.
expected: The socket node survives the SIGKILL; `control list` exits 0, prints `stale control socket removed`, and the node is gone; the restarted owner binds and stops with 0.
health exits 20 and its first line starts `health exit=20 state=fenced reason=starting`; the owner exits 0 on SIGTERM.

The two posts exit 1 with `refused operator post REFUSED from-invalid` and `... REFUSED unknown-group`; the well-formed post exits 0 (`accepted operator post ACCEPTED`); the revoke exits 1 with `refused operator control REFUSED no-such-grant`.
The reply is a kind-2 FNCT frame whose payload is the one octet 1 (:accepted) followed by the SHA-256 trailer; the revoke then exits 0.

scenarios.title: Two friends' nodes peer for days without an operator: a peer that lists an article it cannot produce, a clean restart, pulls every minute (bounded native form: 30 minutes)
steps: S: a scripted reader-only peer listing <real-0>, <ghost>, <real-1> for NEWNEWS since before it was built, serving the real ones and answering ARTICLE <ghost> 430. B: `peer add S ... fn.* - 127.0.0.9 true`, `peer pull S 2 3`.
The same with FN_PULL_TEST_KILL at after-fsync:2 and before-write:2 (round 1's held close), then a restart.
Soak (FN_PULL_SOAK_SECONDS=1800): B pulls a fn node A and S every 60 s with bound 3; A receives an article every two minutes; B restarts cleanly half-way.
expected: Both real ids stored once in round 1; `cursor=held unavailable=1` twice, then `cursor=advanced unavailable=1 dropped=<ghost>` once; the first three NEWNEWS name one instant; three ARTICLE <ghost>.
after-fsync:2: three ARTICLE <ghost> in all (the count survived); before-write:2: four (round 1 not durable); the real ids stored once.
Every article A held stored once at B; <ghost> dropped once; three ARTICLE <ghost>.

scenarios.title: Two agents on two fn nodes peered over NNTP exchange a signed report and a reply across every ownership cut, a repeated transfer, a lost reply and a node restart mid-poll, with one transition each
steps: A authors R into node A; A's feed carries R to B and B's NEWNEWS pull lists it again; an IHAVE of R is offered to B.
A probe consumer on B polls, B restarts, the probe polls again and acks twice.
B's consumer is cut in-transaction, after-commit, at the owner after its ack commits, before Q's POST, and at the owner after Q commits; it wakes after each.
Q crosses to A; A's consumer is cut after its ack and wakes; both consumers wake to their frontiers.
Separately: A's owner accepts R and A's consumer dies before recording the answer; A revokes its author; B consumes R; A wakes.
expected: B's Store holds one article for R (the pull does not fetch it; the IHAVE is answered 435 duplicate).
The same report and cursor bytes are re-served after the restart; the second ack leaves the position unchanged.

B's database holds nothing after the first cut; one transition and one pending reply after the second; the uncertain ack settles by position; the uncertain POST settles by the resend's duplicate answer or store-observation; exactly one transition.

A correlates Q with R in one transition (inbox: repeat for its own R, applied for Q); at each hop the authored source and both signatures equal the submission artifact's, checked with the receiving consumer's keyring; each node holds two articles.
B's one transition; A's resend is refused (revoked) and settles only itself; R is stored by store-observation.

scenarios.title: The four-node mission with relays that serve both directions at once: no listener turns and no direction restarts of the relays
steps: tests/bp-dtn7/run_mission_four_node.py --report signed and --report unsigned on the DTN developer image: A -> X (fn relay) -> dtn7 r1 -> r2 -> Y (fn relay) -> B and back; X and Y run `bp-node serve -` (the listener set: both boundaries bound) with one argv per incarnation.

The only stops: X SIGKILLed while holding (step 2), X down while the receipt crosses (steps 2 to 4), A SIGKILLed (step 4), and the K6 Store writer-lock hand-offs (B stops for its owner in step 5 and serves again for A's receipt in step 6; A stops for its status and owner reads).
--case ambiguous-peer: X's two boundaries on one listener, served on that port explicitly.
expected: 7/7 steps held for both reports; Y is one incarnation for the whole mission; X's three incarnations are the SIGKILL and the outage; every receipt and the reply cross the relay in the opposite direction without a restart.
ambiguous-peer: X refuses A's transfer with reason ambiguous-peer and takes no custody (2/2).

scenarios.title: The 20,000-article chain fixture opens without the quadratic freshness, archive-binding and admission walks, and serves the greeting, GROUP, OVER, ARTICLE and STAT on the opened owner; the reopen from the checkpoint that owner published is timed the same way
steps: Copy hbox:/tank/fn/scratch/fixtures/chain-20000/store (pack-chain-open's fixture, SCN-064; never opened in place) and time `store STORE recover` (peak RSS by /usr/bin/time -v).
Time `operator CONFIG run` to its LISTENING line; on that owner time K greetings each on a fresh socket, GROUP fn.letters, K OVER, K ARTICLE and K STAT by number spread over 1..20000; stop.
Recover and run the same store again (the reopen, from the checkpoint the first run published) and time the LISTENING line, K greetings and GROUP.
Repeat on the image of the lane's base (dev 273cd980) for the before row.
expected: Both images recover 20,000 transactions and 20,000 articles and GROUP answers 211 20000 1 20000 fn.letters; every OVER, ARTICLE and STAT answers 224, 220 and 223.

The lane's image opens in less time than the base image on the same fixture copy (the base: recover 311.9 s, LISTENING 280.7 s on a full replay, the fixture's checkpoint refused by the current format); the numbers and their scope are in the record.

scenarios.title: A store profile whose record bound the consumer poll reply cannot carry is refused by name at init; at the ceiling it is written and served
steps: init with max-record-octets and max-history-octets one octet past 4,294,966,940; then init at 4,294,966,940; start the owner and POST.
expected: The first init exits 1 naming max-record-octets-above-the-poll-reply and writes no config.json; the second writes R 4,294,966,940 and the POST is 240.

scenarios.title: The v1 service envelope of one named profile (scale-1m, 2 KiB articles, one in 256 hybrid-signed) is measured at N = 10,000 on tmpfs and on the ZFS pool and at N = 100,000 on tmpfs: the loaded greeting, OVER, unsigned and signed POST p95, the sustained POST rate on 1 and 8 connections with readers, and the reopen by full replay and from a checkpoint, each row naming its image, box, load and JSON
steps: Preload a scale-1m store to N = 10,000 on tmpfs (`service_envelope.py load`); copy it to tmpfs and to the pool with the derived checkpoint removed (`clone --drop-checkpoint`).

On each copy (`measure --steps latency,checkpoint,restart,rate`, one senv-* unit, MemoryMax=40G, under 30 minutes): the first open (a full replay), 100 greetings, 100 OVERs over 40 and over 100 articles, 100 unsigned and 50 signed POSTs, `store checkpoint`, the open from it, 60 s of closed-loop POSTs on 1 and on 8 connections with 3 ARTICLE readers.

N = 100,000 on tmpfs once: resumable load units, the warm rows on the loading owner, the reopen as the store stands, a fresh checkpoint and the open from it with the rates, the full replay on a copy without the checkpoint.
expected: Every row is recorded with the owner's OWNER-OPEN line, owner CPU, VmHWM, disk octets and inodes, the box load and (ZFS) zfs/zpool state; a row past its time budget says `capped`; a case that cannot run (the 40G ceiling, a unit's 30 minutes) is recorded with why, never replaced by a smaller N.
docs/operator-internals.md publishes the table (docs/operator.md its plain summary) and the weaker tier where storage misses the targets (250 ms p95, 10 POST/s).

scenarios.title: a peer's carried principals grow past the old 1,024 rows by 1,100 separate requests, and a store publishes checkpoint generation 4097 under a profile whose max-transactions admits it
steps: `operator CONFIG init --max-transactions 1164 --max-config-generations 1164 fn.test`; `peer add far ...`; 1,100 separate `peer carries far HEX`; `peer list`.
`peer budget far 1048576 3`; `peer budget far 2097152 5`; `peer list`; `peer carries far HEX0` again; `peer list`.
Developer `store ROOT init --max-transactions 8191`; post; `checkpoint publish`; hard-link generation 0 as generations 1..4096; `checkpoint publish`; `checkpoint status`.
The same with `--max-transactions 4095` and generations 0..4095.

`init --max-group-name-octets 100 fn.test`; `group create` of a 100-octet name, then of a 101-octet name; `init --max-group-name-octets 100` of a 101-octet name on a fresh root; `init fn.test` and `group create` of the 101-octet name.
expected: Every request exits 0; the listing (a fresh open replaying every configuration record) names the 1,100 principals in request order.
Both budget requests exit 0 and the 1,100 principals stay; the repeated principal adds no row.
The second publication prints generation=4097 and status lists 4096 and 4097.
The publication is refused (exit 1) naming the profile's capacity, and the directory is unchanged.

The 100-octet name is created; the 101-octet `group create` exits 1 naming max-group-name-octets with the configuration directory unchanged; the `init` exits 1 naming it and writes no store; under the default profile the 101-octet name is created.

scenarios.title: One served step whose reply is several MiB (the ARTICLE of a 1, 2 and 3 MiB article; an OVER of about 4 MB) is served whole and the owner keeps serving; the exposure's observation of that step decides as over the reply octets
steps: init a store with --max-article-octets 4194304; start the owner; POST articles of 1,048,576, 2,097,152 and 3,145,728 octets and ARTICLE each back on the same connection.
POST 2,000 articles each carrying about 2,000 octets of folded References; GROUP; OVER over the whole group on one connection; STAT on a new connection; SIGTERM the owner.
expected: Each POST is 240 and each ARTICLE is 220 with the posted octets as the stored article's suffix; the owner is still running.

The OVER is 224 with 2,003 lines, more than 3 MiB, and its terminator; the STAT is 223; the owner exits 0. Before PKT-481's fix the 2 MiB ARTICLE and the OVER each stopped the owner with exit 4, `ACL2 error in fn-owner-chunk: Control stack exhausted`.

scenarios.title: An operator reads why an article was withdrawn: `control log` lists the owner's withdrawal record and `control evidence` shows the cancel's decision and the target's withdrawal, live and offline alike
steps: Start an owner with fn.test and control.cancel; enroll a hybrid principal; author a signed target and the same principal's signed cancel of it.
`operator CONFIG control log`; `control evidence` of the cancel, of the target and of an absent Message-ID; `control evidence not-a-message-id`.
Stop the owner; run the same three reports offline.
expected: The target answers 430.

The log prints `withdrawals=1` and one `withdrawal target=... cause=... principal=... scope=- generation=N` line; the cancel's evidence prints `stored=yes txid=N verdict=verified` and `decision=` followed by the log's line; the target's prints `decision=none` and `withdrawn-by ... effect=author`; the absent one `stored=no`; the malformed argument exits 5.
The offline words equal the live words.

scenarios.title: A POST on a store of N committed records reads the count, record octets, completion debt and carriage usage without walking the history: at N=1,000 and N=10,000 x 2 KiB the owner's byte-count term is one record's encoding per POST, and no full re-encoding follows the open
steps: Build the developer profiling image of dev 5c6825b2 (before) and of lane hot-path-scans-2 (after) on hbox, same scripts (planning/evidence/hot-path-scans-2026-09-26/part1-all.sh).

For each image and N in 1,000 and 10,000 x 2 KiB: rep_measure (default profile, K=32, R=3, checkpoint skipped), then reopen the owner on the loaded store and take an sb-sprof :alloc profile over 200 POSTs (allocprof.py).
expected: The profile's samples under the byte-count term (FN-SBUD-RECORD-OCTETS before; FN-SBUD-OCTETS-ADVANCE after) over the 200 POSTs after a reopen: before, the full re-encoding at the first verdict (growing with N); after, about one record's encoding per POST, the same at both N.
Steady-state bytes consed per POST (rep_measure alloc_post) do not grow from the removed terms: the len/nthcdr walks allocated nothing.

scenarios.title: A POST whose statement's key change the Store refused is answered with the 240 naming the refusal; accepted transit lines name their verdict; fn_verify reports revoked against a node that stored an article after revoking its principal; a friend's node holding the inviter at the invitation's keys accepts it by name
steps: Node D (tests.test_native_key_statements): a probe store measures the transactions enrolment, a `keys' grant and one owner start use (U); D is initialised with --max-transactions U+1, P enrolled and granted, then a succession statement signed by P's keys is POSTed, then an ordinary signed article.

Node B: P enrolled, succeeded and revoked by key statements; an article under P's last keys arrives by IHAVE from the configured peer a; HDR :fn-verified; tools/fn_verify.py against B with P pinned at those keys.
The D23 chain (tests.test_native_hybrid_author): an allowlisted relay carries an article to an enrolled sink; both transit log lines are read.

Nodes A5 and B5 (tests.test_native_peer_invite): A enrolled at B and on A, then succeeded (generation 2) on both; A invites B with its current keys and its address; B accepts; B accepts the same invitation again; A confirms.
expected: D's POST reply is exactly `240 article received OK; the key change it carries was refused (key-change-refused)`, the owner log has `key-statement enrol-successor refused`, the next POST is a 441, U+1 transactions are used, and P's history is generation 1 active only.
B answers 235; HDR says `0 revoked P keyring G`; the transit line is `accepted transit ... detail=revoked verdict=revoked ...`; fn_verify exits 1 saying the node revoked P.
The relay's line has ` detail=carried verdict=carried `, the sink's ` detail=none verdict=verified `.

B's accept exits 0 and writes the acceptance; B's log says `peer accept: the inviter's current keys; nothing to enrol`; B's `peer list` names a5.example with A's principal; the second accept is refused `already-enrolled`; A's confirm exits 0; B's history for A is generations 2 (active) and 1 (retired), nothing added.

scenarios.title: The owner's automatic checkpoint publication: after K/2 commits the owner publishes on its own thread through the publication buffer, the file decodes and reopens as the full replay, the verb republishes it byte for byte; under a checkpoint budget the file exceeds the publication is deferred by name, nothing is written, serving continues, the retry waits for the budget, and status names the deferral
steps: A development-profile store (K = 128); an owner; 64 POSTs; connections until the owner logs `CHECKPOINT auto sequence=64 suffix=64 octets=N ms=M'; stop.

`status': open=checkpoint:64 suffix=0 and checkpoint-file octets=N; the observation through four reopening verbs equals the one with the file moved aside (full replay); `store checkpoint' republishes the same bytes.

A fresh store; an owner started with FN_NATIVE_CHECKPOINT_BUDGET_TEST=1024 (developer image: the profile's budget replaced by 1,024 octets; the comparison is ACL2's); 64 POSTs; the deferral line; two more POSTs; no further CHECKPOINT line; `status' while running; stop; `status' offline; a fresh owner under the profile's budget publishes at 66.
expected: The file the owner wrote has exactly the N octets the log named; the checkpoint open serves what the full replay serves; the verb's file is byte-identical.

`CHECKPOINT deferred reason=exceeds-budget estimate=E budget=1024 sequence=64 ms=M' with E > 1024; no checkpoint file; both later POSTs 240; the running `status' prints `checkpoint-file=absent deferred=exceeds-budget estimate=E budget=1024'; offline `status' prints `checkpoint-file=absent' and open=full-replay reason=absent with 66 transactions; the restarted owner logs `CHECKPOINT auto sequence=66 ...' and the next open reads checkpoint:66.

scenarios.title: An owner whose stderr nobody reads keeps serving: 2,000 POSTs are answered and `health` answers with the log lines pending behind the full pipe
steps: Start `operator CONFIG run` with stderr on a pipe the test does not read.
POST 2,000 articles over one NNTP connection; run `operator CONFIG health`.
Read stderr; run `health` until the sink is empty; SIGTERM the owner.
expected: Every POST answers 240; `health` answers (its exit is its first line's) with `log-sink pending=P` and P > 0, and P + dropped + written >= 2,000.
After draining: `pending=0 dropped=0` and written >= 2,000; the owner exits 0; stderr holds at least `written` lines.
On the pre-fix image the same case times out waiting for a POST reply (the owner wedged on the pipe).

scenarios.title: A connection's greeting evaluates no whole-state recognizer: at N = 10,000 and on the 20,000-article fixture the greeting costs milliseconds on the lane's image against hundreds of milliseconds on its base; and a checkpoint written by an image whose event index has an older shape is refused by name and replayed, while the image's own checkpoint is used
steps: On hbox build the developer images of the lane's base (dev a931ed8d) and of the lane (tools/hbox_native.sh; the profiling twin by planning/evidence/served-path-scale-2026-09-26/continuation/prof-build.sh).

Load a 10,000-article store of 2 KiB articles (tools/rep_measure.py on the lane's profiling image, /dev/shm), then on copies of it run greet.py with each image: K = 32 greetings, each on a fresh socket, after 32 warm-up greetings.

Run fixture_open.py (served-path-scale's) over copies of hbox:/tank/fn/scratch/fixtures/chain-20000 with each image: the first open (a full replay), then the reopen from the checkpoint that open published, K = 32 greetings on each.

Recover a copy of the base image's reopened fixture store (its checkpoint has the pair-shaped index) with the lane's image before and after the shape check (`store STORE recover`), and a copy of the lane image's own store.
expected: Every greeting answers 200 or 201; the lane's greeting p95 is milliseconds where the base's is hundreds of milliseconds at the same N on the same box, the box load stated beside each figure.
The pair-shaped checkpoint opens `open=full-replay reason=checkpoint-index-shape` on the image with the shape check, and the lane's own checkpoint opens `open=checkpoint:S`.

scenarios.title: A stranger installs the release tarball, starts a node under the service manager, posts and reads over TLS from another machine, and reinstalls it
steps: Build fn-REV12-linux-x86_64.tar.gz on hbox with packaging/release-tarball.sh from a git archive of REV (FN_CERT_CACHE, FN_ACL2 set).
tools/runpath_check.py --tarball over it; plant a python3 symlink in a scratch copy and run it again.

On hbox under /tank/fn/scratch/release-product: verify SHA256SUMS, unpack, sh fn/install.sh --prefix P --node N --no-service; mission small-community, a self-signed pair, init, policy set path-identity, principal set-password; run under systemd-run --user.
From persvati: STARTTLS, AUTHINFO, POST an article, read it back on a fresh connection.
Stop; remove P; install again from the tarball; start; read the same article from persvati.
expected: The build prints the green-check line, the acquire/validate lines, `version fn REV`, and the runpath check's pass line; the planted copy fails naming bin/python3.
install.sh refuses an existing prefix; the reinstalled node serves the article posted before the reinstall.

scenarios.title: A signed POST's owner CPU does not grow with the retained history: at N = 1,000 and N = 10,000 (32 hybrid-signed carriers in each history) the lane's image spends about the same owner CPU per signed POST, where its base grows about linearly with N
steps: On hbox load a store of N POSTs of about 2 KiB, 32 of them hybrid-signed carriers spread evenly, one hybrid author enrolled (planning/evidence/signed-post-linear-2026-09-26/prof_signed.py load, /dev/shm, profile scale), for N = 1,000 and N = 10,000.

On a fresh copy of each store, open it with the base image (dev 6407de336) and with the lane's image, warm with one unsigned and one signed POST, then time 20 unsigned and 20 signed POSTs, each batch on one connection opened before it, with the owner's CPU (/proc/PID/stat) over each batch (prof_signed.py run).
Profile the base's signed batch with sb-sprof (the profiling twin, --sprof) at both N and name the term that grows.
expected: Every POST answers 240.
The lane's signed POST owner CPU at N = 10,000 is within a small factor of its figure at N = 1,000, and well below the base's at N = 10,000; the box load is stated beside each figure.
The base's profile at N = 10,000 attributes the growth to fn-sf-next-lower under fn-ccar-sn-prepare-identity.

scenarios.title: A POST's owner CPU does not grow with the history through its Message-ID tests: at N = 1,000 and N = 10,000 x 2 KiB the lane's image spends less owner CPU per POST than its base, with the same verdicts, and no Message-ID lookup walks the article list
steps: On hbox take the developer image of the lane's base (dev 6407de336, the throughput gate's native-img-6407de336) and the lane's (tools/hbox_native.sh r1, which also runs tests.test_native_owner).
Load a 1,000-article store of 2 KiB articles (postmeasure.py load) and use the registered 10,000-article fixture /tank/fn/scratch/fixtures/n10k-2k.

For each N and image, on a /dev/shm copy of the store, in its own systemd-run scope: open, one warm-up POST, then K = 400 POSTs of 2,048 octets with the heap hook (bytes consed) and /proc owner CPU around them (postmeasure.py post); alternate the images, five rounds pinned to cores 20-23 (run2.sh); one sb-sprof :cpu window on the lane's image at N = 10,000.
expected: Every POST answers 240; the lane's owner CPU per POST at N = 10,000 is below its base's and near its own N = 1,000 figure, the box load stated beside each figure.

In the lane's CPU profile at N = 10,000, FN-FIND-ARTICLE and FN-ACCEPTEDP have no samples under the POST, and FN-RETAIN-PIN-ID-SCANP (the one remaining admissibility scan, PKT-549) is reached from FN-PIDX-NODE-PREPARE alone, not also from FN-RETAIN-ADMIT.

scenarios.title: OVER over a range costs the rows asked for, not the group's size: at N = 10,000 x 2 KiB OVER 40 rows and OVER 2,000 rows on the lane's image against the perf-ledger's base image, the same fixture, the served bytes identical
steps: On hbox open copies of the fixture /tank/fn/scratch/fixtures/n10k-2k (N = 10,000 x 2,048-octet articles in fn.test; SHA256SUMS there) on /dev/shm with the perf-ledger developer image (dev f314a5a3) and with the lane's developer image (tools/hbox_native.sh), each in its own systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=24G.

planning/evidence/over-number-index-2026-09-26/measure.py reads: GROUP x5, STAT, ARTICLE by number and by Message-ID x32, OVER 1 x32, OVER 40 rows x20, OVER 1-2000 x5, owner CPU per operation from /proc; the SHA-256 of one OVER 1-2000 reply and 32 ARTICLEs by number.
expected: The served-bytes SHA-256 is the same on both images.
OVER 40 rows and OVER 1-2000 fall from hundreds of ms and seconds (rows x N) to tens of ms and under 1 s on the lane image, the box load stated beside each figure.

scenarios.title: A BP bundle's CRC-32C runs the table: on the lane's developer image a bundle of 48 KiB, 256 KiB and 1 MiB encodes and decodes with wire bytes identical to the base image's, and the encode and decode cost about 1 percent of the base's
steps: On hbox, with the base developer image (the perf-ledger's, dev f314a5a3, whose codec books are dev's) and the lane's developer image (tools/hbox_native.sh), load planning/evidence/bp-crc-exec-2026-09-26/bpenc.lisp into each image's raw Lisp with bpenc.sh, back to back on the same box.

For each payload (49,152, 262,144 and 1,048,576 octets) record the guard, encode and decode seconds, the wire length, a digest of the wire computed in raw Lisp (not by the CRC under test) and whether the decode returns the bundle.
expected: The wire length and digest of every payload are the same on both images, and both decode their wire back to the bundle.
The lane's encode and decode are each about 1 percent of the base's at the same payload on the same box, the box load stated beside each figure.

scenarios.title: A served ARTICLE's reply leaves the owner as a range of the octet buffer, byte for byte the reply of the step's effects, at 2 KiB, 32 KiB and 1, 2 and 3 MiB
steps: init a store with --max-article-octets 4194304; start the owner; POST articles of 1,048,576, 2,097,152 and 3,145,728 octets and ARTICLE each back on the same connection (tests/test_native_bounds_join.py LargeReplyTests, the served path now through fn-owner-reply-buffer).
Measure ARTICLE 32 KiB and 3 MiB with a client that reads in 1 MiB chunks: wall, owner CPU and bytes consed per ARTICLE, before and after (planning/evidence/egress-span-2026-09-26/egress.py).
expected: Each ARTICLE is 220 with the posted octets as the stored article's suffix and the owner keeps serving; the bytes are those fn-served-reply-octets of the step's effects decides (fn-served-reply-to-buffer-is-the-reply).
No per-octet cons for the reply on the served read: the ARTICLE's bytes consed fall by at least the reply list and its host copy.

scenarios.title: A POST is served byte-identical after the ingress reads the octet buffer instead of a per-read list: an article of 33 KiB, 200 KiB and 3 MiB is accepted (240) and re-reads identical, and a line split across two socket reads and a dot-stuffed line frame the same article
steps: Init a 4 MiB-article profile; run the owner; POST 33,792 / 204,800 / 3,145,728 octets and re-read each with ARTICLE; POST A+1 octets.
In ACL2: feed a dot-stuffed body line whose CRLF is split across two buffer ranges through fn-wire-feed-span in two reads, and in one read; compare to fn-wire-feed-proper over the octets.

On hbox, the same POSTs (33,792 / 204,800 / 3,145,728 octets, and 200 dot-led lines written in 7-octet pieces) to the span image and to the base image (per-read list, FN_SPAN_REFERENCE_HOST), each on a fresh 4 MiB-article store; ARTICLE each (tests.test_native_bounds_join.SpanReferenceTests).
expected: Each of 33 KiB / 200 KiB / 3 MiB is 240 and re-reads identical; A+1 is refused 441 by size; transactions-used is 3.
The two-read span and the one-read span leave the same wire state and frame the same (:article ((.hi))) event, equal to the reference; a line over the limit closes :line-overlimit at the same octet.
Every POST reply, ARTICLE status line and served article octet agrees between the two images (the injected Date and Injection-Date values masked), and each re-reads the posted body.

scenarios.title: 1,100 separate offline `peer carries` requests on one store cost each request a replay at the records' own work, not the configuration's size per record

scenarios.title: A three-article history with a cancel committed after its target on the live catalog: the pinned reader at the version before the cancel reads the article, a reader who advanced does not, the numbers and Message-ID lookups answer from the tables
steps: tests/acl2/catalog-tests.lisp cat-exec: commit three held rows (two in fn.test, one in fn.test and fn.other), read the Message-ID and number columns, withdraw row 0 at version 3, commit the cancel at sequence 3, read fn-cat-visible-at for versions 3 and 4, redecide row 1, clear.

scenarios.title: A long-lived reader connection sees a peer's new article after its next GROUP, and a cancel committed after the article leaves it visible to that reader until it advances past the cancel (two connections, native)
steps: tests.test_native_reader_freshness (catalog-slice-5, 2026-09-26; the freshness half): a long-lived reader selects the group before the article exists; another connection POSTs (store A) or a peer IHAVEs (store B); the reader's next GROUP reports the new count and its STAT/ARTICLE by Message-ID answer 223/220 as a fresh connection's do (asserted since NNT-042).

tests/acl2/owner-tests.lisp (catalog-slice-5): the reader pinned at version 0 lists the posted article after LISTGROUP and after GROUP and is pinned at the view afterwards; STAT on the reader still at version 0 answers 430 and moves no pin; fn-own-read-repinned says which.

ACL2 half (catalog-slice-2): tests/acl2/catalog-delta-tests.lisp cdt-exec: on the live catalog over the live arena, connection A advances to version 2 before the cancel; the cancel's :withdraw delta and its own row commit; connection B advances to version 3; fn-view-sees at A's and B's versions of row 0 and of the cancel's row.

Cancel-after-target over two native connections (A pinned before the cancel reads the article; A's GROUP; A reads it withdrawn) is 7b's module with the crossed-view arms (PKT-585).
scenarios.expected: A's first read returns the article (223/220), the GROUP reply's count advances, the second read returns 423. ACL2 half: A (version 2) sees row 0 and not the cancel's row; B (version 3) does not see row 0 and sees the cancel's row; a delta does not move A's version.

scenarios.title: An operator describes a group and sets the message of the day on a running node; a new reader connection is shown both, a restart keeps them, and clearing them restores the marker and an empty message
steps: Init a store with fn.test, create fn.live, start the owner; LIST NEWSGROUPS shows the marker for both and LIST MOTD an empty block.

Each refused host is (:refused :listener-unspecified), (:refused :listener-mapped) and (:refused :listener-duplicate) at load; no store is opened.

scenarios.title: A store of another format is refused at open by name: open refused reason=store-format: not an fn store of this release: redeploy fresh, exit 1, the store untouched; the same store with its own profile opens
steps: Synthesize a store of another format (tests/foreign_format_store.py: a fresh store whose config.json is a profile frame naming fn-store-11 under this build's digest, octets pinned to ACL2) and open it with store recover, store status, store inspect, store checkpoint, operator status, operator health and operator run; install a release over a node holding one; put the store's own config.json back and recover.

scenarios.title: store export then store import on a fresh node serves the same history: Message-IDs, numbers, verdicts and consumer cursors equal

On a fresh node: store import DIR (and once with a raised field); start.

scenarios.title: Articles over the protected feed between a Linux node and an OpenBSD node, both from release tarballs: posted on each side, read on the other, and a hybrid-signed carrier crossing once
steps: Start from SCN-090's first two steps with one node on Linux (the release tarball, the system OpenSSL 3) and one on OpenBSD 7.9 (the OpenBSD tarball, base LibreSSL, rc.d), peered by invite, accept and confirm.
Both: a login bound to the other's principal, an FNAUTH1 profile, `peer add` of the same name with `starttls NAME ANCHOR` and both halves (`local.*`); restart both so the new logins are read.
Post one article on each node over STARTTLS; `peer pull` each way.
Enrol the OpenBSD node's own keys there (`hybrid-enroll`), sign an article with them (`hybrid-sign`) and inject it (`hybrid-author`).
Read each article back over STARTTLS on both nodes (raw ARTICLE bytes).
expected: Each origin logs `accepted feed peer=... code=239` and the receiver `accepted transit ... code=239 decision=want`, verdict `unsigned` for the plain posts and `verified` for the signed carrier; each `peer pull` round logs `round=done cursor=advanced transport=tls`.

On the receiving node the article's bytes equal the origin's except the Path line, where the receiver prepended its own path identity with the `!!` diagnostic (RFC 5537 section 3.2.1; RFC 5536 section 3.1.5).
Neither node stops; a fault that stops one is a failure of this scenario, not an environment note.
scenarios.execution_scope: Run once by hand on 2026-09-26: the Linux node on hbox (fn-cde3986a5c78 tarball, OpenSSL 3.3.1) and the OpenBSD 7.9 node in a QEMU guest on hbox (fn-a04213276edf tarball, LibreSSL 4.3.0, 1 vCPU, 2 GiB), OpenBSD-to-Linux carried through an ssh reverse tunnel because the guest's container cannot reach the host's docker bridge address. Not a test module: the log SHA-256s are in the record. One unreproduced stop of the OpenBSD node during the first pulls is PKT-591.

scenarios.title: On a 2 GiB machine a fresh node takes the small preset, serves 100 POSTs, checkpoints and reopens within its figure; the development profile is refused by name at start
steps: Under systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=2G, install bin/fn beside libexec/fn/fn-host (the production image); `operator CONFIG init local.test` with no profile word; `status`.
`run`; POST 100 articles of 2 KiB; ARTICLE the first and last, GROUP and OVER 1-100; wait for `CHECKPOINT auto`; read VmHWM; SIGTERM.
`status` (open=checkpoint); `run` again; ARTICLE and OVER again; VmHWM; SIGTERM.
`init --profile development` through bin/fn; the same store made by the image directly; `run` and `status` through bin/fn.
expected: init writes max-history-octets=8388608; status ends `heap=N MB profile=small machine=2048 MB` with N <= 2048.
Every POST 240; both ARTICLEs 220 with their Message-ID; 211 100; 100 OVER rows; one automatic checkpoint; the owner exits 0.
status says open=checkpoint:S; the reopened owner serves the same; both VmHWM below the limit.
Each is refused, exit 1, `refused machine-cannot-hold-profile heap=H MB machine=2048 MB` with H > 2048, nothing on stdout, no store made by the refused init, nothing listening.

scenarios.title: A read-only group, set offline and live: POST refused by name, LIST ACTIVE status n, a pinned connection unchanged, a restart replays it; and (SEC-006, specified) an unsigned post cancelled by its own login only
steps: `init fn.test`; `group create fn.ro`; offline `group policy fn.absent n` (refused), `group policy fn.ro m` (not accepted), `group policy fn.ro n`.
Start the owner; a reader lists LIST ACTIVE, POSTs to fn.ro, to fn.test,fn.ro and to fn.test, and STATs the refused Message-ID.
Live `group policy fn.ro y`: a new connection lists and POSTs to fn.ro; live `group policy fn.ro n`: another new connection POSTs to fn.ro.
Stop, restart; a reader lists LIST ACTIVE and POSTs to fn.ro.

(SEC-006, specified, not implemented: PKT-575) Logins ember and guest; ember POSTs an unsigned article to fn.test; guest, then ember, POST a cancel of it; a second node relays ember's article and ember's cancel.

After `y` a new connection lists fn.ro y and its POST answers 240; after `n` a new connection's POST to fn.ro answers the read-only 441.
After the restart LIST ACTIVE shows fn.ro n and a POST to fn.ro answers the read-only 441.
(SEC-006, specified) guest's cancel is refused by name and the article stays 220; ember's cancel is accepted and the article answers 430 withdrawn on both nodes, in either arrival order.

scenarios.title: A reader port admits exactly its connection capacity (raised above the old 31, then raised live), refuses the next by name, and exempts the trusted range from the per-address limit, on the developer and production images
steps: Per image: `init fn.test`; `policy set exposure-connections 40`; start the owner on 127.0.0.1; `status`; 40 connections from 127.0.0.1, then a 41st; `health`.
Live `policy set exposure-connections 45`; 5 more connections, then one more; `status`.

Close every connection; live `policy set exposure-per-address 2` and `policy set exposure-trusted 127.0.2.0/24`; 6 connections from 127.0.2.9; 3 from 127.0.3.9; `health`; `policy set exposure-trusted 127.0.2.0/33`; `status`.

The 5 are admitted and the next reads the same 400; status shows connections=45 capacity=45.
