scenarios.title: An INN-shaped peer streams into fn (MODE STREAM, pipelined CHECKs, then TAKETHISes) and gets the IHAVE verdicts in streaming form; fn feeds a 203 peer with CHECK and TAKETHIS and a 501 peer with IHAVE on the same connection
steps: Node T with peer S (inbound fn.*, max-inflight 16). On one connection: MODE STREAM; IHAVE an article (335, 235), IHAVE it again (435), IHAVE an out-of-scope article (335, 437).

Pipeline 20 fresh CHECKs and the held one in one write; TAKETHIS every 238 in one write (PKT-600 repaired, SCN-144); TAKETHIS an out-of-scope article; CHECK the deferred ones in one write and TAKETHIS them in one write; TAKETHIS a held article; CHECK it.
Node A with a streaming peer record to a scripted peer answering MODE STREAM 501: post an article; then to one answering 203.
expected: 203; sixteen 238 then four 431 and 438 for the held one, each echoing its Message-ID; sixteen 239; 439 for the out-of-scope TAKETHIS where IHAVE gave 437; the four deferred now 238 and 239; 439 and 438 for the held article where IHAVE gave 435; every stored article served byte-identical.
The 501 peer receives MODE STREAM then IHAVE on the same connection and never CHECK or TAKETHIS, and a second article reaches it (no stop); the 203 peer receives CHECK then TAKETHIS and never IHAVE.

scenarios.title: The Linux release runs on Debian 12 (glibc 2.36) with only libc and the system libssl: install, init, run, POST and ARTICLE over STARTTLS, stop, SIGKILL, recover
steps: Measure every bundled ELF object's GLIBC version needs (objdump -T, readelf -V, tools/runpath_check.py --tarball).
Rebuild the SBCL runtime with packaging/floor-runtime.sh in debian:12; freeze with FN_FREEZE_RUNTIME; package (release-tarball.sh --runtime-from, or --frozen for a rehearsal).

In a debian:12 container with libssl3 added and nothing else: verify SHA256SUMS, unpack, install.sh --no-service, init, run; from the host, tools/fn_client.py POST and show over STARTTLS; SIGTERM; start; POST; SIGKILL; recover; start; show both.
The same on hbox's own Ubuntu; the unrebuilt tarball's packaging is refused by the runpath check.
expected: No bundled object needs more than GLIBC_2.36; the old runtime is refused naming __isoc23_strtol@GLIBC_2.38 and does not load in debian:12.
Both posts answered 240, both articles served after the SIGKILL and recover, on Debian 12 and on Ubuntu.

scenarios.title: The one resumable checkpoint pipeline: the automatic publication and the verb write the schema-3 tables in batches through the publication buffer, decided by name before any allocation; the file reopens as the full replay and the verb republishes it byte for byte
steps: A development-profile store (K = 128); an owner; 64 POSTs; connections until the owner logs `CHECKPOINT auto sequence=64 suffix=64 octets=N steps=T ms=M' with T >= 4 (one step per table at least); stop.

`status': open=checkpoint:64 suffix=0 and checkpoint-file octets=N; the observation through four reopening verbs equals the one with the file moved aside (full replay); `store checkpoint' republishes the same bytes (`checkpoint sequence=64 octets=N steps=...').

The source assertions: the thread calls fn-ock-next-checkpoint, fn-ockp-setup and the batch loop over the publication buffer; the verb calls fn-store-sco-publish-setup and the same loop; the open loads through fn-sct-load; the cut map is fn-bs-scp-program's, unchanged.

A fresh store under FN_NATIVE_CHECKPOINT_BUDGET_TEST=1024: the deferral line `CHECKPOINT deferred reason=exceeds-budget estimate=E budget=1024', nothing written, serving continues, no retry, `status' carries the deferral; a fresh owner under the profile's budget publishes at 66.
expected: `CHECKPOINT auto sequence=64 suffix=64 octets=N steps=T ms=M' with T >= 4; the file has N octets; the checkpoint open serves what the full replay serves; the verb's file is byte-identical and its line names its steps; the deferral by name with E > 1024, nothing written, serving continues, no retry, `status' carries it, the restarted owner publishes at 66.

scenarios.title: A kill between two pipeline steps reopens with the old checkpoint (the `created' cut's verdict) and the staged file is swept by the writer's recover
steps: A development-profile store; an owner; 64 POSTs; the automatic publication at 64 (the old checkpoint, its digest kept); stop.
An owner under FN_NATIVE_CHECKPOINT_BATCH_FAULT=0:kill; 64 more POSTs; the owner is killed by its publication thread after the first step's frames were written.

The old checkpoint's bytes are unchanged; `status' reads open=checkpoint:64 suffix=64; `recover' sweeps the staging orphan; a fresh owner publishes at 128 and the next open reads open=checkpoint:128 suffix=0.
expected: The owner under FN_NATIVE_CHECKPOINT_BATCH_FAULT=0:kill dies after its first step; the old checkpoint's digest is unchanged; `status' reads open=checkpoint:64 suffix=64; `recover' leaves staging empty; the restarted owner publishes at 128 and the next open reads checkpoint:128.

scenarios.title: A reader reads a cross-posted article's overview: the Xref field names the node's path-identity and the article's local number in every group that holds it, and LIST OVERVIEW.FMT names Xref:full
steps: Init a store with fn.test, create fn.alt, set policy path-identity news.example.org, start the owner.
Post one article to fn.alt, then one cross-posted to fn.test and fn.alt.
A reader: LIST OVERVIEW.FMT; GROUP fn.test; OVER 1-100; XOVER 1-100; OVER; OVER <msgid>; GROUP fn.alt; OVER 1-2; ARTICLE <msgid>.
expected: LIST OVERVIEW.FMT lists the seven fields then Xref:full.
Each OVER line has nine fields; the ninth is 'Xref: news.example.org' then fn.test:1 and fn.alt:2 for the cross-post, fn.alt:1 for the other; the message-id form numbers the line 0.
ARTICLE shows no Xref header (the stored octets).

scenarios.title: A certificate renewal reaches a running node by `tls reload`: new connections get the new certificate, an open session keeps working, and a mismatched key or a dropped name is refused by name with the old certificate still served
steps: `store init fn.test`; certificate A (SAN localhost) at tls/cert.pem and tls/key.pem; `run` with protected_only and a control socket; a reader completes STARTTLS and stays open; `status`.
Replace both files with pair B (SAN localhost, reload.localhost) by rename; a new reader handshakes; `tls reload`; a new reader handshakes; the open reader sends DATE; `status`.
Replace the key with one from another pair; `tls reload`; a new reader handshakes.
Install pair D (SAN localhost only); `tls reload`; a new reader handshakes; the open reader sends QUIT.
With no owner running, `tls reload`.
expected: The first reader is served A; `status` prints `tls names=localhost not-after=YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.

Before the reload the new reader is still served A; `tls reload` exits 0 and prints `tls names=localhost,reload.localhost not-after=...`; the next reader is served B; the open reader's DATE answers 111; `status` prints B's names.
`tls reload` exits 1 with `refused operator tls key-mismatch`; the new reader is served B.
`tls reload` exits 1 with `refused operator tls names-dropped`; the new reader is served B; QUIT answers 205 and the owner is still running.
The command exits non-zero and is not accepted.

scenarios.title: A hostile network is thrown at a running node: malformed command lines, header and body abuse, connection floods and slowloris, pipelining and transit storms, and raw TCPCL/BP abuse; the node stays up, answers a clean session throughout, holds memory bounded, and refuses every ill-formed input by name
steps: Start a scratch loopback owner under systemd-run (MemoryMax=8G) on the developer image; never the live node.
Per family (malformed, header, body, connection, pipelining, transit, bp) send bounded adversarial traffic and log the first line the node returned.

After each family run the oracle: a clean authenticated GROUP/DATE/LIST session answers, the owner is alive with RSS under the profile's heap figure, no served request exceeded the wall bound, and the service log holds no fault.
For BP, drive a bp-node serve listener with wrong TCPCL magic, a never-completing contact, and an XFER_SEGMENT declaring a 4 GiB payload with tiny data.
expected: Every malformed command line is refused 501; header/body abuse is refused 441 by a distinct named reason or accepted only when valid (a supplied Path is injected per NNT-012); a connection flood is refused 400 past the capacity and slowloris is closed silently at the timer; 1000 pipelined DATEs all answer and non-peer TAKETHIS/CHECK/IHAVE are refused 502; the bp-node answers an oversized XFER_SEGMENT with MSG_REJECT and does not preallocate the declared length.
The node never crashes, never hangs past its bounds, never grows memory without bound, and answers a clean session correctly after every family.
scenarios.execution_scope: Executed on hbox (developer image, code-identical to dev b4b343d51) against a scratch loopback owner and bp-node under systemd-run MemoryMax=8G. All seven families green, no defects. Not exercised: transit interior abuse (announced sizes, million-id promises, pipelined TAKETHIS/PKT-600) from an authenticated peer session (a non-peer connection is uniformly refused 502; the peer path is covered by SCN-138); a real 100 MiB body under a peer feed; TLS-port handshake garbage on 563 (no TLS listener configured in this run).

scenarios.title: The TLS surface of a running node is thrown hostile traffic on 563 (implicit TLS) and 119 (STARTTLS): garbage before and mid handshake, a hello with no cipher, TLS 1.0/1.1 only, an oversized record, plain NNTP on the TLS port, STARTTLS-then-plain-then-STARTTLS, an unsolicited client cert, an unserved SNI, alert and close_notify floods, a TLS-layer slowloris, and a full-handshake burst; the node refuses each by a named TLS alert or 502, serves a clean session throughout, and holds memory bounded
steps: Start a scratch loopback owner under systemd-run (MemoryMax=8G) on the dev-HEAD developer image, configured with a self-signed [listener] tls_cert/tls_key pair and a tls_port; never the live node.

Against the implicit-TLS port and the STARTTLS path, send the tls family: garbage before/mid handshake, a ClientHello with no cipher and a NULL cipher, TLS 1.0 and 1.1 only offers, a 16 KiB+1 record, plain NNTP on the TLS port, STARTTLS then plain then STARTTLS again, STARTTLS then garbage, an unsolicited client certificate, SNI for an unserved name, an alert flood, a close_notify storm, and a 200-way TLS slowloris.
Measure the handshake CPU cost: 300 sequential handshakes and a 30 s 48-way full-handshake burst, reading the owner's /proc CPU and thread count.

Run the oracle: a clean plaintext session answers, the owner is alive with RSS under the heap figure, no served request exceeded the wall bound, the service log holds no fault, the second STARTTLS is 502, a reader is served during the flood, and the implicit-TLS listener still answers afterward.
expected: Every hostile handshake is refused by a named TLS alert (record_overflow, illegal_parameter, handshake_failure, protocol_version, unexpected_message) or held to the 10 s deadline and closed; plain NNTP on the TLS port leaks no reply; the second STARTTLS is 502; unsolicited client certs and unserved SNI complete and are ignored (single cert served).

The node never crashes, hangs, or grows memory without bound; RSS stayed 585 MB under a 2,819 MB heap figure; steady-state node CPU 2.467 ms per handshake. Two host-level gaps are filed as packets: TLS handshakes are not metered by the exposure kernel (PKT-639) and TLS refusals are logged only to stderr, not the service log (PKT-640).
scenarios.execution_scope: Executed on hbox against the dev-HEAD developer image 6701d5753 (system libssl OpenSSL 3.3.1) and probed against a LibreSSL node on the OpenBSD VM, both loopback under systemd-run MemoryMax=8G; never the live node. TLS family green, no crash/hang/leak/fault; two host-level packets filed (PKT-639 unmetered handshakes, PKT-640 refusals not in service log). Not exercised: a real TLS 1.3 KeyUpdate flood (an encrypted post-handshake record, not forgeable with the standard library); the OpenBSD implicit-TLS (563) port (the VM node ran STARTTLS only).

scenarios.title: An offline configuration request authorizes from the fold its open computed: 300 separate `peer carries` requests timed against the image before PRF-209
steps: `operator CONFIG init`; `peer add far ...`; FN_PEER_ROWS_REQUESTS=300 separate `peer carries far HEX`, timed, on the image before and after PRF-209 on the same box; `operator CONFIG group create` answers `verification=VERIFIED` (tests.test_native_admin).
expected: Every request exits 0 and the listing names the principals in request order; the total time is recorded before and after (planning/evidence/config-consumer-catalog-2026-09-26.md).

scenarios.title: Pipelined articles: eight TAKETHIS in one write from a streaming peer, and two POST blocks in one write from a reader, are each committed and answered in order
steps: Node T with peer S: eight TAKETHIS commands with their articles in one write; QUIT.
Node T with peer S: four TAKETHIS with no CHECK, sent as small TCP_NODELAY segments cut every 7 octets and inside every .CRLF terminator.
Node P, no peer: two POST blocks in one write; POST, then the article and the next POST in one write, then the last article and QUIT in one write.
expected: Eight 239s in order, each echoing its Message-ID, then 205; all eight stored byte-identical.
Four 239s in order, each echoing its Message-ID, then 205; all four stored byte-identical.
340 240 340 240 340 240 340 240 205 in that order (no 340 before the 240 of the article preceding it); all four stored.

scenarios.title: Power is cut to the block device under a committing node (dm-log-writes, ext4) at 1,281 write boundaries across POST commits, checkpoint capture, compaction, reclaim, a near-full store and a recovery cut again; every acknowledged POST is served byte-identical afterwards, no refusal becomes acceptance, no binding or number moves
steps: On hbox (Linux 6.11): a data and a log loop device under dm-log-writes, ext4 on the mapped device; the developer image's node on it (scale profile, small open suffix): init, POSTs with a mark in the log after every 240 and every known 441 refusal, two store compactions, retention set released-by-all-holders, store reclaim; references read from the uncut store to /dev/shm.

For each cut (an entry of the log and a mode: flush, prefix, subset of unflushed writes, or 4096-octet tears), rebuild the device, mount, e2fsck, recover, store inspect the lost-reply POSTs, start the owner, ARTICLE and OVER everything, re-POST the newest acknowledged Message-ID and a fresh one, status; rerun compact or reclaim for their cuts; for a fifth of the cuts, cut the recovery again under a second log.
Control cuts judge a POST whose writes all follow the cut as acknowledged; each must be caught. A barrier=0 run shows the fsync assumption is load-bearing.
scenarios.expected: No acknowledged POST missing or changed, no refused POST served, lost-reply POSTs whole or absent, recover/owner/status without fault, bindings and numbers stable, reclaim accounting whole, every control caught; on barrier=0 acknowledged POSTs are lost (the assumption broken, not fn).

Drain one contact, asking before every offer, with the head scan (fn-bpnj-contact-next) and with the cursor (fn-bpnjc-contact-next), driving each offer's outcome.
Count the job records each drain's asks examine and time both drains and the transitions alone (tools/bench/bp-drain-bench.lisp).
expected: Both drains offer the same N jobs in the same order.
The cursor's asks examine N records in all (the head scan's about 2N^2), and the cursor drain's wall less the transitions' is a small constant share.

scenarios.title: Articles of 2,000,000 lines and of one 4 MiB line are posted, served (ARTICLE, BODY), reopened and served again byte-identical at 1 MiB of control stack per thread and at the image's own 64 MiB, on the production and developer images
steps: init a store with --max-article-octets 8388608; start the owner with SBCL_USER_ARGS=--control-stack-size 1MB; POST an article of 2,000,000 body lines (every sixteenth a lone dot), ARTICLE and BODY it; POST an article whose body is one line of 4,194,304 octets and ARTICLE it; SIGTERM.
start the owner at the image's own stack on the same store (the reopen); ARTICLE both again; POST a second 2,000,000-line article and ARTICLE it; SIGTERM.
start the owner at 1 MiB again (a second reopen); ARTICLE the second article; SIGTERM.
expected: Every POST is 240; every reply is the status line, the stored article exactly dot-stuffed (RFC 3977 section 3.1.1) and the terminator, ending with the posted body; BODY has 2,000,002 CRLFs; the owner exits 0 each time. Before this lane the 2,000,000-line POST exhausted the stack in fn-post-body-octets and the 4 MiB line in fn-wire-list-length (Control stack exhausted in fn-owner-chunk-span).
The replies at 64 MiB are byte-identical to those at 1 MiB; the second article is served.
The reply at 1 MiB after the reopen is byte-identical to the one at 64 MiB.

scenarios.title: Two accounts with different access, four local consumers over a mixed stream: each bound consumer is served only its account's groups, with its account's password; the unbound one everything; cursors survive a restart; a widened rule resumes a refused consumer without a skip; on both images
steps: `init local.general`; `group create fn.public`, `group create fn.private.x`; start the owner (implicit TLS, protected_only); invite and redeem alice and bob; `account access bob --read 'fn.*,!fn.private.*' --post 'fn.*'`.

`fn consumer bootstrap`; register bob-pub (fn.public), bob-priv, alice-priv and operator (fn.private.x); `consumer bind bob-pub --account 'b b'` (refused); bind bob-pub and bob-priv to bob, alice-priv to alice; `consumer show`.

bound-poll bob-pub with a wrong password; plain poll of bob-pub; bound-poll of the unbound operator; bound-poll bob-priv; bound-poll alice-priv with bob's password.
bob-pub bound-poll (pub1), bound-ack with a wrong password, plain ack, bound-ack; alice-priv bound-poll (secret1, not acked); restart the owner.

Drain bob-pub, alice-priv (bound) and operator (plain); bound-poll bob-priv; `account access bob --read '*' --post '*'`; drain bob-priv; `consumer unbind bob-pub`; bound-poll and plain poll of bob-pub.

Run pooled account Begin/Tick with genuine owner-control ticket; interleave the frontier before authority begin, retain exact candidate/input after durable begin, refuse changed input, and perform actual account alias-return epilogue before ATS finish.
Refuse actual native account adoption with no installed control binding before entropy I/O or constructors; refuse a new account reservation while CURRENT holds configuration acquiring3/source10.

Exercise actual typed C publication transport: retain acquisition effects before one preparation quantum, resume the same source without acquisition, and preserve pending/full8/lease roots until genuine journal completion.

Park a yielded typed C claim, refuse parking with any registered journal intent, then resume on a genuine newer receipt from the same control slot; inject unavailable source, budget yield, wrong slot and unknown source.
expected: The malformed binding exits non-zero; `consumer show` prints `consumer bob-pub account bob` and `consumer alice-priv account alice`. It contains no pending invitation or redeemed-account line.
Every refusal in step 4 exits 1 and writes no cursor.
bob-pub is served pub1; the wrong-password and plain acks exit 1, the bound ack 0.

After the restart: bob-pub pub2, cross; alice-priv secret1 (re-served), secret2, cross; operator secret1, secret2, cross; bob-priv refused, then after the widened rule secret1, secret2, cross (nothing skipped); unbound bob-pub: bound-poll exits 1, plain poll an empty page.
Source/candidate shape never grants allocation or authority; uncertainty retains original/produced roots, and ATS:left never settles account lifetime.

Both refusal paths retain all original effects and spend no account PRS identity; an existing configuration continuation requires its retained receipt, never a candidate-ID bypass. Negative recording evidence does not qualify funded lifecycle.

C preparation yield, refusal and recovery remain distinct; pending result never publishes or invokes E alias-clear. Original BODY must cover the whole C closure; C suspended-claim resume and durable/alias receipts remain unqualified.

Original token/demand/roots/reservation survive; only phase/output or original intent slot/nonce change. No account PRS reissue, reselect, refund or E clear occurs. Source unknown fences. These actual-source recording paths remain unfunded and unqualified.

scenarios.title: Power is cut (qemu SIGKILL) under an OpenBSD 7.9 node while a client outside the VM posts, compacts, captures checkpoints, reclaims, initializes, imports and recovers; after reboot, fsck, recover and the owner, every acknowledged article answers exactly as first read, a refused one stays refused, local numbers are never reassigned
steps: Clone the release-openbsd VM and install the release under test (tools/power_loss_openbsd.py install NAME TARBALL; first run fn-a04213276edf, the continuation fn-c5d7b5b3fd9f); give it a store disk (raw: completed writes survive the cut; qcow2 writeback: unflushed allocations are lost) with FFS1 or FFS2; the node listens on the guest loopback behind a pf redirect.

Per epoch: `operator init` cut at a random point, then cycles of: boot, `fsck -y`, mount, `operator recover`, the owner, the oracle (ARTICLE of every attempted Message-ID, OVER), `status`, then the phase's work and a SIGKILL of qemu: posting on two connections (every seventh POST names an uncarried group), posting across the automatic checkpoint capture, `store compact` with the owner stopped, an interrupted `recover`, `store export` (owner stopped) then `store import` of that archive into a second store ROOT2, cut, and `retention set released-by-all-holders` then `store reclaim`.

expected: recover exits 0, the owner reaches LISTENING, status exits 0 after every cut.
Every 240 answers 220 with the posted body and headers, byte-identical at every later cut until a reclaim starts; every 441 answers 430; an attempt with no reply answers 220 (then pinned) or 430.
A local number once observed keeps its Message-ID; a newly listed article takes a number above every number observed before.
A rerun of an interrupted compact or reclaim succeeds; after a completed reclaim every article answers 430.

After an init cut the store is absent (at most one ROOT.init-*, which the next init names as interrupted-init, and init succeeds once it is removed) or the complete empty store (status 0, transactions=0); after an import cut ROOT2 is absent (at most one ROOT2.import-*, named by the next import, which then succeeds) or the complete imported store (the exported transaction count, sampled `store inspect` answers equal the source's).

steps: `init local.general`; `group create fn.alice`, `group create fn.bob`; start the owner (implicit TLS and STARTTLS, protected_only); invite and redeem alice and bob; `account access LOGIN --read fn.LOGIN --post 'fn.*'` for each; bootstrap; register alice-inbox (fn.alice) and bob-inbox (fn.bob); bind each to its account.
alice-inbox and bob-inbox each `bound-wait --timeout 60`; after 4 s alice posts to fn.bob; 2 s after bob's wait returns, bob posts to fn.alice; bob acks.
bob-inbox `bound-wait --timeout 3`; bob-inbox with alice's password.
Twelve bob-inbox waits; a thirteenth; a post to fn.bob; ack.
Restart the owner; bob-inbox wait 3 s; alice-inbox wait.
fn_agent: alice next/ack; alice posts `question` to fn.bob; bob next, reply --group fn.alice, ack; alice next, ack; bob next --timeout 1.
expected: bob's wait exits 0 with for-bob within 5 s of the 240 while alice's still sleeps; alice's then exits 0 with for-alice within 5 s.
The 3 s wait exits 0 with an empty report after at least 3 s; the wrong password exits 1 at once.
The thirteenth exits 1 at once; the post wakes all twelve with for-all.
After the restart bob's wait times out empty (his ack kept); alice's answers for-alice again (not acked: at-least-once).

bob's next prints the question as JSON (Message-ID, groups, From, Subject, body); the reply is accepted; alice's next prints it with the question's Message-ID in References; bob's last next prints {"kind": "empty"}.

scenarios.title: The batch's crash cuts (log-written, log-fenced, finish per member): an acknowledged member's record is in every admissible image's scan, an unacknowledged one may be absent and is never answered durable
steps: Prepare a batch of three members against one catalog (fn-owb-take within log-batch-records and log-batch-octets), append it (fn-owb-append: the kernel's batch becomes the batch in flight and the store's pending list is the segment's one write) and fence it (fn-owb-fence); acknowledge the first member (fn-owb-finish-member).

Take the crash image at each cut: after the append (log-written: every admissible selection over the pending write, fn-bs-crash), after the barrier (log-fenced) and after each member's finish; recover each image (fn-owb-recover, fn-lgk-recover) and scan its content.

Remove each hypothesis of T1 in turn (the alignment, R at the cut, the admissible image, the platform's tear) with a ground witness of the conclusion's failure; label the corrupted-state witnesses separately.
expected: At log-written the scan reads the committed records then a prefix of the batch (fn-lg-crash-verdictp); at log-fenced and after every finish it reads the committed records and the whole batch; the acknowledged member's record is in every image's scan (fn-owb-acknowledged-record-survives-crash).
A member not yet acknowledged may be absent after a log-written crash and is answered :durable by no cut before the barrier; a member acknowledged before the cut is absent from no image.
Every removed hypothesis has a witness whose conclusion fails, with the retained hypotheses checked affirmatively.

scenarios.title: The fsync error: every member of the batch is uncertain, the store is fenced, and recovery admits the committed records then a prefix of the batch
steps: Prepare and append a batch of three members; answer the barrier :eio under an admissible selection over the pending write (fn-bs-fsync-file bs ino (cons :eio choices)); apply fn-owb-fence-failed to the layer.

Read the layer's words (fn-owb-fault-words) and attempt fn-owb-finish-member; recover the kernel from the store the failure left (fn-lgk-recover of its durable content) and compare with the committed records and the batch in flight, for each admissible selection.
Retry the barrier on the same store (fn-bs-refence-after-error-fences-nothing) and read the words again.
expected: The kernel is :fault; every member in flight or waiting is answered :uncertain and none :durable; the finish acknowledges nothing (fn-owb-fence-failed-answers-uncertain).

The recovered kernel holds the committed records followed by a prefix of the batch in flight under every admissible selection (fn-owb-uncertain-batch-recovers-to-a-prefix); the store stays fenced until recovery (STO-004).
The retry fences nothing further and answers no member the failed barrier covered :durable.

scenarios.title: The snapshot page store: a commit writes only fresh pages and one record, a crash at every cut opens on the committed or the previous state, other roots and forks are untouched, allocation answers fresh addresses and reclamation never frees the reserved page or a page a valid record keeps
steps: Build store D0 (root :main, one commit: directory at 6, one table page at 1 naming two data pages at 2 and 3, a stale page at 4; page 0 reserved; allocator FREE (5 4), HWM 7). Commit one dirty page (pgs-plan-commit, pgs-commit) and open it eagerly and lazily (pgs-open); grow it across a table-page boundary (341 to 343 logical pages).
Take the crash image at every host cut (pgs-cut-crash-point over *pgs-snapshot-cuts*, each write landed or not, the record old, torn or new; pgs-crash) and open each image in both modes.
Fork :main to :b (pgs-fork) and commit on each; commit on :main with an allocator state that violates pgs-alloc-inv.
Allocate singles and a directory run in each of pgs-alloc's three branches (one-page run, a run in FREE, a run at HWM).

Run a reclamation cycle started before a second commit and one started after it: on the model (pgs-reclaim over pgs-disk-keeps) and on the executable cycle the host runs (pgs-g-start, which marks the reserved page, pgs-g-load-free0-all, pgs-g-mark-run-all and pgs-g-mark-words-all per record, pgs-g-sweep-all in quanta, pgs-g-install).

Remove each keystone hypothesis in turn (no open, dirty pages out of order, no allocator invariant, a forged record, r2 = r, a colliding digest, marks missing a kept address, marks missing the reserved page, FREE0 flags missing a free address) with the retained hypotheses checked affirmatively; label the corrupted-state witnesses separately.
expected: The committed open answers the next txid and the dirty pages applied (pgs-open-after-commit); the plan writes the data page, the table page and the directory to fresh addresses and the record to the older slot.

Every cut opens on the committed or the previous state, the previous one unless the new record landed; a missing page is refused by name (:page-damaged, :table-damaged, :dir-damaged, :commit-torn) in both modes (pgs-open-after-crash).
A commit on one root leaves every other root's open unchanged (pgs-crash-isolates-other-roots, pgs-fork-denotes); without the allocator invariant another root's open changes.
Every allocation answer is distinct and no valid record of any root keeps it (pgs-alloc-fresh).

The sweep frees exactly the dead record's directory, table page and replaced data page, never the reserved page 0 and never a page the surviving record keeps; the executable cycle's installed free list keeps pgs-alloc-inv (pgs-reclaim-never-frees-live, pgs-g-reclaim-sound).
Every removed hypothesis has a witness whose conclusion fails.
